clusters.title: Large Multi-Functional Regulatory Supercluster: Transcription, RNA Processing, Ubiquitin-Proteasome, Signaling, and Cytoskeletal Organization
clusters.overall_function: This very large cluster encompasses a broad array of cellular regulatory functions including transcriptional regulation (Mediator complex, TAF/TFIID, SAGA, PRC1/2, NuRD, NELF), RNA processing and splicing (hnRNPs, SRSF, snRNPs, CELF, MBNL, RBM families), ubiquitin-proteasome system (FBXO/FBXL/FBXW F-box proteins, USPs, RNFs, UBE2/3/4 enzymes, CUL1/4/5), signal transduction (MAP3K/MAPK, PI3K/AKT/mTOR via RPTOR/RICTOR, STAT family, Rho GEFs/GAPs, Wnt/beta-catenin via CTNNB1/AXIN), cytoskeletal and actin dynamics (MYO family, DIAPH, WASF, ARPC, FMNL), autophagy (ATG genes, WIPI1, RUBCN), vesicle trafficking (VPS, TRAPPC, SNX, AP complexes), DNA damage response (CHEK2, NBN, MDC1, XRCC1, RAD21, PARP family), and chromatin remodeling (KDM, SETDB, SMYD, ARID, PHF families). The cluster likely represents a co-regulated gene network active in proliferating or differentiating cells rather than a single coherent pathway.

qc_warnings: Cluster is extremely large (2231 genes), strongly suggesting over-aggregation or insufficient resolution in the clustering algorithm
Multiple distinct biological programs are co-clustered: neuronal, muscle, germline, immune, and ubiquitous housekeeping functions

Presence of tissue-restricted genes (TNNI1-3, TNNT1-3, RYR1/2, PIWIL1/2/4, DAZL, HORMAD1/2, HBA1/HBA2/HBZ/HBM/HBQ1) alongside broadly expressed regulatory genes is a major QC concern suggesting mixed cell type contamination or batch effects
Hemoglobin genes (HBA1, HBA2, HBM, HBQ1, HBZ) in a large regulatory cluster is suspicious and may indicate red blood cell contamination or ambient RNA
Germline/piRNA pathway genes (PIWIL1/2/4, DAZL, BOLL, HORMAD1/2, TEX11) co-clustering with ubiquitous transcription factors is biologically implausible in most somatic contexts
The cluster likely reflects a catch-all bin for genes not fitting tighter clusters rather than a coherent co-expression module
clusters.rationale: The 2231-gene cluster centered on MYO9A contains an extraordinarily diverse set of gene families. Core regulatory machinery (Mediator, TFIID/TAF, SAGA, PRC1/2, NuRD, NELF, spliceosome, hnRNPs, ubiquitin E3 ligases, deubiquitinases) is broadly expressed and could co-cluster due to shared housekeeping expression patterns. However, the simultaneous presence of highly tissue-restricted programs—cardiac/skeletal muscle contractile proteins (TNNI, TNNT, TMOD, LMOD, RYR, CACNB), erythroid hemoglobins (HBA1/2, HBM, HBQ1, HBZ), germline piRNA/meiosis genes (PIWIL1/2/4, DAZL, HORMAD1/2, BOLL, TEX11), and neuronal synaptic genes (DLG1-4, MAGI2, UNC13A/B, NOVA1/2, STMN1-4)—is a strong indicator that this cluster is not biologically coherent. It likely represents an artifact of low clustering resolution, batch effects, or ambient RNA contamination mixing multiple cell type transcriptomes. The oncogenic and signaling components (CTNNB1, STAT3, MYCN, BRAF, PIK3CB, RPTOR/RICTOR) are real and functionally related but are diluted by the tissue-specific noise. Confidence is moderate-low due to the implausible co-clustering of mutually exclusive tissue programs.
recommended_followups: Re-cluster at higher resolution to split this supercluster into biologically coherent sub-modules (e.g., splicing, ubiquitin, mTOR, muscle, neuronal, germline)
Check for ambient RNA contamination (SoupX or similar) given hemoglobin gene presence
Perform pathway enrichment (GO, KEGG, Reactome) on sub-sampled gene sets to identify dominant functional themes
Assess whether tissue-restricted genes (HBA1/2, TNNI1-3, PIWIL1/2/4) show correlated expression or are outliers within the cluster
Use UMAP/tSNE of cluster member expression profiles to identify sub-structure and potential batch confounders
Validate key hub genes (CTNNB1, STAT3, RPTOR, SUZ12, PRPF8) as cluster anchors by examining their co-expression neighborhoods independently

clusters.title: Large Cytoskeletal Scaffold, Signaling Hub, and Cell Division Regulatory Network
clusters.overall_function: This very large cluster encompasses a broad but interconnected set of biological functions centered on cytoskeletal organization, cell polarity, scaffold/adaptor signaling, centrosome/cilia biology, cell division and mitosis, DNA damage response, apoptosis regulation, immune signaling, and vesicle trafficking. Key themes include: (1) extensive cytoskeletal scaffolding via AKAP, CCDC, ANKRD, and PDZ-domain proteins; (2) centrosome/centriole/cilium assembly (CEP family, CFAP family, CCDC39/40, DNAAF proteins); (3) mitotic regulation (BUB1, CENP family, TACC, HAUS, PLK4, STIL, ASPM, KNL1, SGO1/2, INCENP, NUSAP1); (4) Rho/Rac GEF-GAP signaling (ARHGEF/ARHGAP families); (5) DNA damage and repair (BRCA1/2, FANCA/F/M, ATM pathway components, RMI1, SLX4); (6) apoptosis/BCL2 family; (7) immune/NF-kB signaling (IRAK1/2, IRF3/4/7/8/9, CARD family, STING1, NFKB inhibitors); (8) meiosis (SYCP1-3, SYCE, TEX genes, STRA8, MEI1/4); (9) vesicle/membrane trafficking (RAB11FIP, DENND, TBC1D, SNX families).
cell_type_relevance: Cycling/proliferating cells: strong mitotic and centrosome gene signature (CEP family, HAUS, TACC, CENP, BUB1, PLK4, STIL, ASPM, NUSAP1, PTTG1/2)
Immune cells (B/T/myeloid): IRF4/8, SPI1/SPIB, CARD9/10/11, IRAK1/2, STING1, BLNK, LAT, FYB1/2, INPP5D, NCF1/4, CD14 suggest myeloid and lymphoid programs
Meiotic/germ cells: SYCP1-3, SYCE1/3, TEX genes, STRA8, MEI1/4, SPATA genes, TSGA10 strongly indicate germ cell/meiotic state
Ciliated cells: CFAP family, DNAAF1/3/8, CCDC39/40, DNAH14, RSPH genes, TEKT genes, ODAD1/3 indicate motile cilia
Neurons/synaptic cells: SHANK1-3, SYNGAP1, SYT family, HOMER1/3, DLGAP1-5, RIMS1-4, SNAP91 indicate neuronal/synaptic identity
cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Testis/gonad: large meiotic and spermatogenesis gene block (SYCP, SYCE, TEX, SPATA, TSGA, SPEM, CFAP, TEKT) strongly points to testicular germ cell origin
Brain/neural tissue: SYT family, SHANK, HOMER, DLGAP, SYNGAP1, RIMS, SNAP91, RTN1-4, SNCA/B/G suggest neural tissue
Immune/hematopoietic tissue: IRF4/8, SPI1, CARD11, BLNK, LAT, CD14, INPP5D, NCF1/4 suggest hematopoietic compartment
Epithelial/polarized tissues: PARD3/6, PATJ, SCRIB, MARVELD2/3, CGN, CGNL1, TJP3 suggest epithelial polarity programs
Broadly proliferative tissues: centrosome/mitosis genes are tissue-nonspecific markers of proliferation
cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: Germ cell tumors: meiotic gene expression (SYCP, TEX, SPATA, STRA8) is a hallmark of testicular germ cell tumors and some seminomas
Hematologic malignancies: IRF4/8, SPI1/SPIB, CARD11, BCL10, BLNK, INPP5D are key drivers/markers in B-cell lymphomas, AML, and related cancers
Highly proliferative cancers: CEP, TACC3, PLK4, ASPM, NUSAP1, PTTG1/2, BUB1, KIFC1 are overexpressed in many aggressive solid tumors

Neuroblastoma/neural tumors: SNCA, SYT, SHANK, HOMER genes may mark neural lineage tumors
cell_malignancy_status_prediction_releva: Malignant cells likely marked by: overexpression of mitotic/centrosome genes (PLK4, TACC3, ASPM, NUSAP1, PTTG1/2, BUB1, KIFC1, STIL) which are broadly upregulated in cancer vs normal
DNA damage response genes (BRCA1/2, FANCA/F/M, RMI1, SLX4, RBBP8, CLSPN, TICRR) may indicate replication stress common in malignant cells

drug_sensitivity_relevance: PLK4/STIL/ASPM/TACC3 overexpression: sensitivity to centrosome-targeting agents (centrinone/PLK4 inhibitors, TACC3 inhibitors)
BRCA1/2/FANCA pathway: sensitivity to PARP inhibitors and platinum-based chemotherapy (homologous recombination deficiency)

qc_warnings: Cluster is extremely large (2074 genes), strongly suggesting over-aggregation or insufficient resolution in the clustering algorithm

Biologically heterogeneous: contains at least 5-6 distinct functional modules (meiosis/germ cell, centrosome/mitosis, immune signaling, neuronal/synaptic, cytoskeletal scaffolding, DNA repair) that would normally be expected to separate into distinct clusters
High proportion of uncharacterized/poorly annotated genes (C#orf, FAM, CCDC, PRR, NUTM2 families) may be inflating cluster size artificially
Presence of both highly tissue-specific genes (SYCP3, SHANK1, CD14) and broadly expressed scaffolding genes suggests possible batch effect or embedding artifact pulling disparate programs together
Many CCDC (coiled-coil domain containing) genes may cluster together due to shared domain architecture rather than shared biological function, representing a technical artifact
Large number of PRR (proline-rich) and FAM genes with unknown function reduces interpretability and confidence
Mixed immune + meiotic + neuronal + mitotic signatures in one cluster is biologically implausible for any single cell type, suggesting this cluster should be split
clusters.rationale: The cluster of 2074 gene symbols is dominated by several recognizable biological themes: (1) centrosome/cilia biology via the CEP, CFAP, CCDC, and DNAAF gene families; (2) mitotic regulation via CENP, HAUS, TACC, BUB1, PLK4, STIL, ASPM, KNL1, SGO1/2, INCENP, NUSAP1; (3) meiosis/spermatogenesis via SYCP1-3, SYCE1/3, TEX genes, SPATA genes, STRA8, MEI1/4; (4) Rho GTPase signaling via extensive ARHGEF/ARHGAP families; (5) immune signaling via IRF3/4/7/8/9, CARD9/10/11/14, IRAK1/2, STING1, SPI1/SPIB, BLNK, LAT; (6) neuronal/synaptic function via SYT family, SHANK1-3, HOMER1/3, DLGAP1-5, RIMS1-4; (7) DNA damage response via BRCA1/2, FANCA/F/M, SLX4, RMI1; (8) apoptosis via BCL2L1, MCL1, BAX, BID, BMF. The co-clustering of these diverse programs in a single cluster of >2000 genes is biologically implausible for any single cell type and strongly suggests over-clustering, insufficient embedding resolution, or shared low-level features (coiled-coil domains, proline-rich regions, scaffold/adaptor architecture) driving spurious co-clustering. The cluster has value as a broad 'signaling scaffold and cell biology' module but should be computationally subdivided for meaningful biological inference.
recommended_followups: Re-cluster at higher resolution to split this mega-cluster into biologically coherent sub-clusters (meiotic, mitotic/centrosome, immune, neuronal, cytoskeletal)
Perform gene ontology enrichment analysis to identify dominant GO terms and assess whether sub-modules can be separated

Validate immune sub-module (IRF4/8, SPI1, CARD11, BLNK) against known immune cell type marker databases (CellMarker, PanglaoDB)

Examine batch effects and embedding quality metrics to rule out technical artifacts driving this large cluster

clusters.title: Cancer-Testis Antigens, Reproductive/Germline Genes, and Tissue-Restricted Repeat Families
clusters.overall_function: This cluster is dominated by cancer-testis antigens (CTAs: MAGE-A/B/C/D/E/F/H, GAGE, PAGE, XAGE, SAGE, TSPY, VCX/VCY families), germline/testis-specific genes (DAZ1-4, SPATA31, TEX, FANK1, GCNA, CYLC2, TXNDC2), and tissue-restricted structural/secreted proteins (amelogenins AMELX/AMELY/AMBN/AMTN/ENAM/DSPP/DMP1/MEPE for enamel/dentin; salivary proteins HTN1/HTN3/STATH/PRB/SMR3; mucins MUC7/MUC12/MUC16/MUC17; skin barrier FLG/FLG2/IVL/HRNR/RPTN/CRNN/SBSN; milk caseins CSN1S1/CSN2/CSN3). Large repeat-gene families (ANKRD, GOLGA6/8, NBPF, SPDYE, SPATA31, LRRC37A) and pseudogenes inflate the cluster. Secondary components include cell-cycle inhibitors (CDKN2A/B/C/D), ASB E3 ligase adaptors, and ARMCX/GPRASP X-linked neuronal genes.
cell_type_relevance: Spermatogonia and male germ cells (DAZ1-4, TSPY, GCNA, CYLC2, FANK1, SPATA31, VCX/VCY)
Epidermal keratinocytes / skin barrier cells (FLG, FLG2, IVL, HRNR, RPTN, CRNN, SBSN, CDSN)

cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Testis/germline: strongest signal from DAZ, TSPY, SPATA31, TEX, GCNA, VCX/VCY, CYLC2

CDKN2A/B loss is a hallmark of many cancers (glioblastoma, melanoma, pancreatic); co-clustering with CTAs may reflect shared epigenetic derepression in aggressive tumors

MUC16 (CA-125) is a canonical ovarian cancer marker; MUC12/MUC17 are expressed in GI cancers

cell_malignancy_status_prediction_releva: CTA re-expression (MAGE, GAGE, PAGE, XAGE) is a strong indicator of malignant or epigenetically derepressed cells; normal somatic cells are largely CTA-negative

drug_sensitivity_relevance: MAGE-A3/A4/C2 and other CTAs are targets for T-cell receptor (TCR)-engineered T-cell therapies and cancer vaccines; CTA-high tumors may be candidates for immunotherapy

perturbation_modeling_relevance: CTA genes (MAGE, GAGE, PAGE) are frequently included in cancer perturbation screens as epigenetically regulated targets; their re-expression upon DNMT/HDAC inhibition is a useful readout

qc_warnings: Cluster is extremely large (392 genes) and biologically heterogeneous — likely reflects co-regulation by shared epigenetic mechanisms (germline/CTA derepression) rather than a single pathway or complex

Massive expansion of repeat-gene families (ANKRD20A pseudogenes, GOLGA6/8 paralogs, NBPF, SPDYE, SPATA31, LRRC37A) may reflect sequence similarity-driven co-clustering or annotation artifacts rather than functional coherence

Tissue-restricted structural genes (amelogenins, caseins, salivary proteins, skin barrier) are biologically unrelated to CTAs and germline genes — their co-clustering is suspicious and may indicate batch effects, low-expression noise, or embedding artifacts in the source data
Pseudogenes (ANKRD20A2P, ANKRD20A3P, ANKRD20A4P, GOLGA8DP, TSPY9P, SPDYE10P, SPDYE12P) should not be co-clustered with functional genes without justification

IGHD (immunoglobulin D diversity) gene segments (IGHD1-1, IGHD1-7, etc.) and TCR diversity segments (TRBD1, TRDD1-3) are V(D)J recombination loci — their presence may indicate B/T cell contamination or genomic locus co-regulation artifacts
Mixed lineage signals (germline, dental, skin, salivary, mammary, immune) strongly suggest this cluster should be split or reviewed for technical confounders
clusters.rationale: The cluster's core identity is cancer-testis antigens and germline-restricted genes, which share epigenetic silencing in normal somatic tissues and reactivation in cancer. The MAGE, GAGE, PAGE, XAGE, SAGE, TSPY, VCX/VCY, DAZ, and SPATA31 families are canonical CTAs or testis-specific genes. However, the cluster also contains large blocks of tissue-restricted structural proteins (amelogenins, caseins, salivary proteins, skin barrier proteins) that are biologically unrelated to CTAs. These likely co-cluster due to shared low/absent expression in most cell types (creating similar embedding vectors) or due to genomic proximity and repeat-family expansion. The massive representation of repeat-gene paralogs and pseudogenes further inflates the cluster and reduces functional coherence. CDKN2A/B/C/D co-clustering with CTAs is notable and may reflect shared chromosomal or epigenetic regulatory contexts in cancer. Overall, the cluster has a recognizable CTA/germline core but is contaminated by unrelated tissue-specific and repeat-family genes, warranting sub-clustering and QC review.
recommended_followups: Sub-cluster the 392 genes to separate: (1) CTA/germline core, (2) repeat-gene families, (3) tissue-restricted structural genes, (4) pseudogenes
Check whether tissue-restricted genes (amelogenins, caseins, salivary) show correlated expression in the source data or are co-clustered due to near-zero expression across most samples
Assess whether CDKN2A/B co-clustering with CTAs reflects a cancer-specific epigenetic derepression signature
Remove or flag pseudogenes and V(D)J loci before downstream functional analysis
Run enrichment analysis (GO, KEGG, Hallmark) on the CTA-only subset to confirm germline/immune evasion signatures
Validate CTA gene expression patterns against known CTA databases (CTdatabase, CTAtlas) to confirm cluster identity

clusters.title: Olfactory Receptor Gene Family Cluster
clusters.overall_function: This cluster is composed almost entirely of olfactory receptor (OR) genes, members of the largest gene family in the human genome. These are G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) that detect odorant molecules and transduce chemosensory signals in the olfactory epithelium. The cluster spans multiple OR gene subfamilies (OR1-OR14) and includes a small number of pseudogenes and a lncRNA (LINC02203).
cell_type_relevance: Olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs) of the olfactory epithelium — each OSN expresses a single OR gene under monoallelic, singular OR gene choice mechanisms
Sustentacular/supporting cells of the olfactory epithelium may show low-level OR expression
Ectopic OR expression has been reported in non-olfactory tissues (e.g., sperm, gut, kidney) but at low levels; bulk co-expression of hundreds of ORs is atypical outside olfactory tissue
Cluster may reflect olfactory epithelium or olfactory neurosphere-derived cell populations in single-cell data
cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Strong predictor of olfactory epithelium or olfactory bulb tissue origin
May indicate nasal mucosa or olfactory neurosphere-derived samples

If detected in non-olfactory tissue, likely reflects genomic co-regulation artifacts, batch effects, or ambient RNA contamination
cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: Olfactory neuroblastoma (esthesioneuroblastoma) — a rare malignancy of the olfactory epithelium — could express OR genes
Some OR genes have been reported upregulated in prostate, colorectal, and other cancers, but coordinated expression of hundreds of ORs in a single cancer cell type is not well established
Low confidence for most cancer types; may serve as a lineage marker for olfactory-lineage tumors
cell_malignancy_status_prediction_releva: In olfactory tissue context, high OR expression is consistent with normal olfactory sensory neurons rather than malignant cells

clusters.title: Kinase Signaling & RNA-Binding Protein Network
clusters.overall_function: This cluster encompasses a large, functionally diverse but interconnected set of serine/threonine kinases (spanning CDKs, MAPKs, CAMKs, PKCs, PAKs, PLKs, AURKs, SIKs, MARKs, NEKs, SGKs, RPS6Ks, and many others) alongside a broad array of RNA-binding proteins (hnRNPs, SR proteins, PABPs, ELAVL/HuR family, MSI, IGF2BPs, PTBPs, RBMs) and splicing factors (SRSFs, U2AF, SF3B subunits, SRRM). The kinases collectively regulate cell cycle progression, stress responses, cytoskeletal dynamics, and signal transduction, while the RNA-binding proteins control mRNA splicing, stability, translation, and export. A subset of kinases (SRPK2/3, CLKs, DYRK1A/B) directly phosphorylate SR splicing factors, providing a mechanistic bridge between the two functional groups. Phosphatases (PPP1CA/B/C, PPP2CA/B, PPP4C, PPP6C) and scaffolding/adaptor proteins (STRADB, TOLLIP, TRIB1-3) are also present.

clusters.title: Small Transmembrane Protein Superfamily: Tetraspanins, Claudins, FXYD, MS4A, ZDHHC, and Related Membrane Proteins

Collectively these proteins are involved in membrane organization, cell-cell adhesion, ion channel regulation, lipid metabolism, vesicle trafficking, and palmitoylation-dependent protein targeting. clusters.title: Immunoglobulin and T-Cell Receptor Variable Gene Segments (Adaptive Immune Receptor Repertoire)

clusters.title: Calcium-Binding Proteins, Myosin Light Chains, S100 Family, and Mitochondrial Carriers (SLC25A)
clusters.overall_function: This cluster is dominated by three major functional groups: (1) EF-hand calcium-binding proteins spanning multiple subfamilies (calmodulins, S100 proteins, calbindins, parvalbumins, neuronal calcium sensors, CABP family, KCNIP/KChIPs, recoverin/GUCA family, calcineurin regulatory subunits); (2) myosin light chain proteins (MYL family) involved in muscle contraction and cytoskeletal regulation; and (3) the nearly complete SLC25A mitochondrial carrier family responsible for metabolite transport across the inner mitochondrial membrane. The co-clustering of these groups likely reflects shared EF-hand domain architecture and/or co-expression patterns rather than a single unified biological pathway.

clusters.rationale: The cluster is anchored by KDM5B (a histone H3K4 demethylase) but contains 1885 genes spanning virtually every major cellular process. Coherent sub-modules are identifiable: (1) a chromatin/epigenetic module (KDM1A/B, KDM2A/B, KDM4B-F, KDM5A-D, EZH2, HDAC1, BRD2-4, BRDT, KAT5/6A/6B/7/8, SMARCA1/2/4/5, CHD1-6, PHF10/14/20); (2) a DNA replication/repair module (MCM3-8, PCNA, POLA1, POLD1, RAD51, BRIP1, XRCC3, TOP1/2A/2B, FEN1, MUS81); (3) a metabolic supermodule spanning fatty acid oxidation (ACADL/M/S/SB, HADH, HADHB, EHHADH), TCA cycle (CS, IDH1/2, OGDH, SDHA/B, FH, MDH1/2), glycolysis (ALDOA/B/C, GAPDH, LDHA/B, PKM, PFKM/P), amino acid catabolism (HAL, TAT, PAH, CPS1, OTC, ASS1, ASL), and nucleotide biosynthesis (IMPDH1/2, GMPS, PPAT, CAD, DHODH, TYMS); (4) a cytoskeletal module (MYH1-15, KIF1A-21B, DNAH1-17, SEPTIN1-14, SPTA1/B, SPTBN1-5, FLNA/B/C); (5) an immune kinase module (LCK, FYN, ZAP70, SYK, BTK, ITK, TEC, TXK, JAK1/3, TYK2, SRC, YES1, BLK, HCK, FGR, FER, FES, FRK, MATK, SRMS). clusters.title: Voltage-Gated and Ligand-Gated Ion Channel Superfamily
clusters.overall_function: This cluster is dominated by ion channel subunit genes spanning multiple families: voltage-gated calcium channels (CACNA1*), voltage-gated sodium channels (SCN*), voltage-gated potassium channels (KCNA/B/C/D/F/G/H/J/K/MA/NN/NQ/NS/NV), HCN channels, nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (CHRNA/B/D/G), GABA-A receptors (GABR*), glycine receptors (GLR*), serotonin 5-HT3 receptors (HTR3*), TRP channels (TRPC/TRPV), CNG channels (CNGA/B), and KCTD proteins (potassium channel tetramerization domain). Together these genes encode the core machinery of electrical excitability, synaptic transmission, and ion homeostasis in excitable cells.

clusters.title: Cornified Envelope, Keratin-Associated Protein, and Terminal Differentiation Gene Cluster

clusters.title: WD40 Repeat Protein Superfamily: Ubiquitin-Proteasome, Chromatin, Cilia, and Ribosome Biogenesis
clusters.overall_function: This cluster is dominated by WD40 repeat-containing proteins (WDR family) and associated scaffold/adaptor proteins involved in diverse cellular processes including ubiquitin-mediated protein degradation (DCAF/CRL4 E3 ligase adaptors, FBXW F-box proteins, FZR1/APC/C), chromatin remodeling and epigenetic regulation (EED/PRC2, RBBP5/MLL, DDB2/NER), ribosome biogenesis and RNA processing (UTP4, UTP18, PWP2, WDR75, NLE1, RRP9), ciliogenesis and IFT (IFT80, IFT140, IFT172, WDR19, WDR35), and cell cycle regulation (CDC20, CDC20B, FZR1). The WD40 domain serves as a versatile protein-protein interaction scaffold unifying these functionally diverse members.

clusters.rationale: The cluster is unified by the WD40 beta-propeller repeat domain, a versatile protein-protein interaction scaffold. The majority of members (>60%) carry 'WDR' nomenclature or are known WD40-containing proteins. Functional annotation reveals at least four major sub-modules: (1) CRL4/SCF ubiquitin E3 ligase adaptors (DCAF family, FBXW family, DDB2, WSB1/2), (2) chromatin/epigenetic complexes (EED/PRC2, RBBP5/MLL, GRWD1), (3) intraflagellar transport and ciliogenesis (IFT80/140/172, WDR19/35, CFAP genes, POC1A), and (4) ribosome biogenesis/RNA processing (UTP4, UTP18, PWP2, WDR75, NLE1). The co-clustering is plausible as a domain-family cluster but is functionally heterogeneous. Key outliers include GNB1-5 (G-protein beta subunits, also WD40), PAFAH1B1 (LIS1, WD40), and EML family (EMAP-like, WD40-related). The representative gene EML2 is consistent with the WD40 theme. No obvious batch or stress artifact signatures are apparent, but the functional breadth warrants sub-clustering.

clusters.title: Kelch/BTB-domain ubiquitin substrate adaptors, annexins, and phosphatases
clusters.overall_function: This cluster is dominated by three functionally related but distinct protein families: (1) Kelch-like (KLHL) and BTB-domain proteins that serve as substrate-recognition adaptors for Cullin3-RING E3 ubiquitin ligase complexes, mediating targeted protein degradation; (2) Annexins (ANXA), calcium- and phospholipid-binding proteins involved in membrane organization, vesicle trafficking, and anti-inflammatory signaling; and (3) Dual-specificity phosphatases (DUSPs) and related phosphatases (PTP4A, PTPN, PTPRR) that dephosphorylate and inactivate MAP kinases and other signaling intermediates. Together these families converge on regulation of protein homeostasis, signal transduction attenuation, and membrane dynamics.

clusters.rationale: The cluster is anchored by a near-complete set of human CC and CXC chemokines, which form a coherent secreted immune signaling module. However, the co-clustering of the entire actin superfamily (including chromatin-remodeling actin-related proteins), cystatin protease inhibitors, HSPA chaperones, and liver-derived plasma proteins suggests that the clustering algorithm may have grouped these based on shared sequence/structural features (small secreted proteins, high expression) or embedding proximity rather than strict functional coherence. The chemokine core is biologically coherent and highly relevant to immune cell biology, TME characterization, and drug targeting. The non-chemokine members represent likely contamination or over-aggregation artifacts that should be investigated.
recommended_followups: Sub-cluster the 93 genes to separate the chemokine module from actin, cystatin, HSP, and plasma protein sub-groups
Check whether actin-related proteins (ACTL6A/B, ACTR1A/B, ACTR2) cluster with BAF/chromatin remodeling complexes in other analyses
Validate co-expression of chemokines with actins in single-cell RNA-seq data to determine if co-clustering reflects genuine co-expression or embedding artifact
Assess batch effects: HSPA1A/HSPA1B upregulation may indicate heat shock or dissociation stress in scRNA-seq data
Perform pathway enrichment on the chemokine-only subset to confirm immune recruitment and TLS signatures
Investigate plasma protein genes (AHSG, KNG1, HRG) for hepatocyte contamination in non-liver datasets

clusters.title: Immunoglobulin and T-cell Receptor Joining Segments (J-genes)
clusters.overall_function: This cluster comprises exclusively V(D)J recombination joining (J) segment genes from all major adaptive immune receptor loci: immunoglobulin heavy chain (IGHJ), immunoglobulin kappa light chain (IGKJ), immunoglobulin lambda light chain (IGLJ), T-cell receptor alpha (TRAJ), T-cell receptor beta (TRBJ), T-cell receptor delta (TRDJ), and T-cell receptor gamma (TRGJ). These are the germline-encoded J-segment gene segments that contribute to the CDR3 junction region of antigen receptors through somatic recombination, generating antigen receptor diversity.
cell_type_relevance: B cells (all stages: pro-B, pre-B, immature B, mature naive B, memory B, plasma cells) — express IGH/IGK/IGL J-segments after VDJ recombination
T cells (all stages: thymocytes, naive T, effector T, memory T) — express TRAJ/TRBJ/TRDJ/TRGJ segments
Innate-like lymphocytes: gamma-delta T cells (TRDJ/TRGJ), NKT cells (TRAJ18 is canonical iNKT), MAIT cells (TRAJ33/TRAJ20/TRAJ12 are canonical MAIT)
Cycling lymphocyte progenitors undergoing VDJ recombination in bone marrow or thymus
cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: High expression of IGHJ/IGKJ/IGLJ genes suggests B-cell-rich tissues: bone marrow, lymph node, spleen, tonsil, blood
High expression of TRAJ/TRBJ genes suggests T-cell-rich tissues: thymus, blood, lymph node, spleen
Mixed IGH+TCR J-segment expression may indicate lymphoid organs or peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs)
Presence of TRDJ/TRGJ suggests gamma-delta T cell compartments: gut epithelium, skin, liver
cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: B-cell malignancies: B-ALL, CLL, DLBCL, follicular lymphoma, multiple myeloma — clonal IGH/IGK/IGL J-segment usage
T-cell malignancies: T-ALL, peripheral T-cell lymphoma, CTCL — clonal TRAJ/TRBJ usage
Gamma-delta T-cell lymphoma — clonal TRDJ/TRGJ usage
MAIT cell or iNKT cell lymphoma — specific TRAJ usage (TRAJ33, TRAJ18)
Clonal restriction of a single J-segment in a cell population is a hallmark of malignant lymphocyte expansion
cell_malignancy_status_prediction_releva: Polyclonal J-segment usage across many genes suggests non-malignant reactive lymphocyte populations
Monoclonal or oligoclonal J-segment usage (single dominant J-gene) is a strong indicator of malignant or clonally expanded lymphocytes
This cluster's expression profile could be used to infer clonality and thus malignancy status in lymphoid tumors
Non-lymphoid malignant cells (carcinomas, sarcomas) would not express these genes, so their presence marks lymphoid identity
drug_sensitivity_relevance: BCR signaling inhibitors (ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib — BTK inhibitors) are relevant for B-cell malignancies with clonal IGH/IGK/IGL usage
PI3K-delta inhibitors (idelalisib) relevant for B-cell lymphomas
Anti-CD20 (rituximab), anti-CD19 (tafasitamab), CAR-T targeting B-cell antigens — relevant in IGH/IGK/IGL-expressing malignancies
TCR-pathway inhibitors and checkpoint immunotherapy relevant for T-cell malignancies with clonal TRAJ/TRBJ usage
Clonal J-segment identity can inform neoantigen-based or TCR-targeted therapies
perturbation_modeling_relevance: J-segment genes are non-coding in the traditional sense (they are recombined genomic segments); perturbation of individual J-genes is not straightforward in standard CRISPR screens
However, expression levels of J-segment transcripts can serve as proxies for lymphocyte activation, differentiation state, and clonality in single-cell perturbation experiments
In AIVC/GEARS-style models, this cluster would serve as a lymphocyte identity signature rather than a perturbable pathway
Useful as a co-variate or cell-type annotation feature in perturbation atlases to identify contaminating or infiltrating lymphocytes
Recombination activating genes (RAG1/RAG2) perturbation would affect J-segment usage indirectly
qc_warnings: All 92 entities are immunoglobulin or TCR J-segment genes — this is a highly coherent and biologically meaningful cluster

The co-clustering of B-cell (IGH/IGK/IGL) and T-cell (TRA/TRB/TRD/TRG) J-segments in a single cluster may reflect shared sequence/structural features of J-segments rather than co-expression in a single cell type — this is a potential concern for expression-based clustering

If this cluster was derived from expression data, co-expression of both B-cell and T-cell receptor J-segments in the same cells would be biologically unusual (except in very early lymphoid progenitors or due to ambient RNA/doublets)
In scRNA-seq data, high J-segment expression may reflect ambient RNA contamination from lysed lymphocytes in non-lymphoid samples
Absence of V and D segment genes from this cluster is notable and may indicate a deliberate or algorithmic separation of J-segments from other VDJ components
clusters.rationale: All 92 gene IDs are unambiguously immunoglobulin (IGHJ1-6, IGKJ1-5, IGLJ4-7) and T-cell receptor (TRAJ1-61, TRBJ1-1 to TRBJ2-7, TRDJ1-4, TRGJ1-2, TRGJP/P1/P2) joining segment genes. These are the germline J-gene segments used in V(D)J recombination to generate antigen receptor diversity. The cluster is biologically coherent as a set of J-segments, but the mixing of B-cell and T-cell receptor loci suggests the clustering criterion may be sequence similarity or genomic feature similarity rather than co-expression in a single cell. In expression-based single-cell data, this pattern could arise from ambient RNA, doublets, or early lymphoid progenitors. The cluster is highly informative for lymphocyte identity, clonality assessment, and adaptive immune receptor repertoire analysis.
recommended_followups: Determine whether clustering was based on sequence similarity, genomic annotation features, or expression correlation — this affects biological interpretation
In scRNA-seq context, check for doublets or ambient RNA contamination if both IGH and TCR J-segments are co-expressed in single cells
Use J-segment expression to annotate lymphocyte subtypes and assess clonality in tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte studies
Separate B-cell (IGH/IGK/IGL) from T-cell (TRA/TRB/TRD/TRG) J-segments for lineage-specific downstream analyses
Cross-reference with V and D segment clusters to reconstruct full VDJ recombination context
Apply TCR/BCR repertoire analysis tools (e.g., scTCR-seq, scBCR-seq, TRUST4, MiXCR) to quantify clonality from these J-segment expression patterns

clusters.title: Cadherin Superfamily Cell Adhesion Molecules
clusters.overall_function: This cluster comprises members of the cadherin superfamily, including classical cadherins (CDH1/E-cadherin, CDH2/N-cadherin, and others), desmosomal cadherins (DSC1-3, DSG1-4), protocadherins (clustered PCDHA, PCDHB, PCDHG subfamilies and non-clustered PCDHs), FAT atypical cadherins, CELSR/Flamingo cadherins, and DCHS cadherins. These are calcium-dependent cell-cell adhesion molecules involved in tissue morphogenesis, epithelial integrity, neuronal connectivity, planar cell polarity, and cell identity specification.
cell_type_relevance: Epithelial cells: CDH1 (E-cadherin) is a canonical epithelial marker; DSC/DSG desmoglein/desmocollin genes mark stratified epithelium and keratinocytes
Neurons and neural progenitors: CDH2 (N-cadherin), clustered protocadherins (PCDHA/B/G), CELSR2/3, and non-clustered PCDHs are highly expressed in neurons and involved in synaptic specificity
Cardiomyocytes and muscle: CDH15 is expressed in muscle; DSG2 and DSC2 are prominent in cardiac desmosomes
Hepatocytes and intestinal epithelium: CDH17 is a liver/intestinal cadherin marker
Skin keratinocytes: DSG1, DSG3, DSC1, DSC3 are hallmarks of epidermal differentiation
cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Brain/neural tissue: large representation of clustered protocadherins (PCDHA, PCDHB, PCDHG) and CELSR/FAT cadherins strongly suggests neural origin
Epithelial tissues (gut, liver, kidney, lung): CDH1, CDH16, CDH17, CDH6 are tissue-restricted epithelial cadherins
Skin/epidermis: desmosomal cadherins (DSG1-4, DSC1-3) point to epidermal or stratified epithelial origin
Kidney: CDH16 is a kidney-specific cadherin
Cardiac tissue: DSG2, DSC2 are prominent in cardiac intercalated discs
cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: Epithelial cancers (carcinomas): CDH1 loss is a hallmark of EMT in breast, gastric, colorectal, and other carcinomas; CDH2 upregulation marks mesenchymal/EMT state
Glioma and neural tumors: protocadherins and CELSR genes are expressed in brain tumors and may mark neural cancer cell states
Squamous cell carcinoma: DSG1-3, DSC1-3 mark squamous differentiation programs in head and neck, lung, and skin SCC
Hepatocellular carcinoma: CDH17 expression is associated with liver cancer
Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy: DSG2/DSC2 mutations are linked to this cardiac malignancy-adjacent condition
cell_malignancy_status_prediction_releva: CDH1 (E-cadherin) downregulation is a strong indicator of malignant EMT transition and invasive phenotype; its expression may help distinguish non-malignant epithelial from malignant mesenchymal-like cells
High expression of clustered protocadherins may mark non-malignant neurons or well-differentiated neural tumors
Loss of desmosomal cadherins (DSG/DSC) can indicate dedifferentiation in epithelial cancers
FAT4 is a known tumor suppressor; its loss may mark malignant cells in multiple cancer types
Overall, the cluster contains both tumor suppressor (CDH1, FAT4) and context-dependent oncogenic (CDH2) members, making it useful for EMT and differentiation state scoring
drug_sensitivity_relevance: CDH1 loss/EMT status correlates with resistance to EGFR inhibitors and sensitivity to certain mesenchymal-targeting agents
CDH2 (N-cadherin) expression is associated with resistance to endocrine therapy in breast cancer and targeted therapies in melanoma; ADH-1 (N-cadherin antagonist) has been explored clinically
Desmosomal cadherin expression patterns may predict sensitivity to agents targeting epidermal differentiation pathways
FAT4 loss may sensitize cells to Hippo pathway-targeting agents
Protocadherin expression patterns in neural tumors may correlate with response to temozolomide or other CNS-directed therapies
perturbation_modeling_relevance: CDH1 knockout is a classical EMT-inducing perturbation; modeling CDH1 loss predicts downstream vimentin/fibronectin upregulation and invasiveness programs
CDH2 overexpression perturbation models mesenchymal transition
FAT4 loss-of-function perturbation activates Hippo/YAP signaling, relevant for GI and neural cancers
Clustered protocadherin diversity (PCDHA/B/G) makes them interesting targets for combinatorial perturbation studies of neuronal identity
CELSR2/3 perturbations model planar cell polarity disruption relevant to neural tube defects and cancer invasion
DSG2/DSC2 perturbations model desmosome disruption relevant to cardiac and epithelial disease models
qc_warnings: The cluster spans multiple cadherin subfamilies with distinct tissue expression patterns (neural vs. epithelial vs. cardiac), which may reflect broad co-regulation at the chromatin/transcriptional level rather than co-expression in a single cell type

The large number of clustered protocadherins (PCDHA1-13, PCDHB1-16, PCDHGA/GB/GC) may dominate the cluster due to their genomic clustering and co-regulation, potentially biasing functional interpretation toward neural contexts
FREM2/FREM3 (FRAS1-related extracellular matrix proteins) are included and are not classical cadherins; their presence may indicate slight boundary imprecision in clustering
No obvious housekeeping gene contamination detected
Mixed lineage signal (neural + epithelial + cardiac) warrants caution when applying this cluster as a single functional unit in cell type prediction
clusters.rationale: The cluster is dominated by cadherin superfamily members: classical type I/II cadherins (CDH1, CDH2, CDH6-CDH24), desmosomal cadherins (DSG1-4, DSC1-3), clustered protocadherins (PCDHA1-13, PCDHAC1-2, PCDHB1-16, PCDHGA1-12, PCDHGB1-7, PCDHGC3-5), non-clustered protocadherins (PCDH8-11X/Y, PCDH20), FAT cadherins (FAT2-4), CELSR/Flamingo cadherins (CELSR2-3), and DCHS cadherins (DCHS1-2). All share the cadherin EC domain architecture and calcium-dependent adhesion function. The inclusion of FREM2/FREM3 is a minor anomaly. The clustering is biologically coherent at the superfamily level, likely driven by shared domain architecture, co-regulation, or co-expression in tissues with high adhesion complexity (brain, epithelium). The large protocadherin representation reflects their genomic clustering and shared regulatory elements.
recommended_followups: Perform tissue-specific expression analysis to determine whether the cluster is driven by neural, epithelial, or multi-tissue co-expression patterns
Assess whether FREM2/FREM3 should be reassigned to an extracellular matrix cluster
Use this cluster for EMT scoring by focusing on CDH1 vs CDH2 ratio as a continuous EMT axis
Evaluate clustered protocadherin subset (PCDHA/B/G) separately for neural cell type classification
Test FAT4 and DCHS1/2 as Hippo pathway proxies in cancer perturbation models
Validate desmosomal cadherin sub-signature (DSG1-4, DSC1-3) as a squamous differentiation marker in cancer cell type prediction

clusters.title: C1q-domain Superfamily and Collagen Extracellular Matrix Proteins
clusters.overall_function: This cluster is dominated by two major protein superfamilies sharing the C1q/TNF-related globular domain: (1) classical complement C1q subunits and C1q-domain-containing proteins (C1QTNF family, CBLN family, ADIPOQ, MBL2, COLEC10/11, SFTPA1/2/D, COLQ, ERFE, GLDN, OTOL1, C1QL1-4, CD70), and (2) fibrillar and non-fibrillar collagens (COL1A1/2, COL2A1, COL3A1, COL4A1-6, COL5A1-3, COL7A1, COL8A1/2, COL9A1-3, COL10A1, COL11A1/2, COL13A1, COL15A1, COL16A1, COL18A1, COL21A1, COL22A1, COL23A1, COL25A1, COL27A1, COL28A1). The unifying structural feature is the homotrimeric or heterotrimeric assembly via collagen triple-helix and/or C1q globular head domains, reflecting shared evolutionary origin and structural homology. Functionally, members span ECM scaffolding, complement activation, adipokine signaling, innate immunity, synaptic organization, and surfactant biology.
cell_type_relevance: Fibroblasts and myofibroblasts: high expression of fibrillar collagens (COL1A1, COL1A2, COL3A1, COL5A1)
Chondrocytes: COL2A1, COL9A1-3, COL10A1, COL11A1/2 are hallmark cartilage matrix genes
Adipocytes: ADIPOQ, C1QTNF family members are adipokines enriched in adipose tissue
Macrophages/monocytes: C1QA, C1QB, C1QC are classical markers of tissue-resident macrophages and monocyte-derived cells
Alveolar type II pneumocytes: SFTPA1, SFTPA2, SFTPD are surfactant proteins specific to lung epithelium
Cerebellar granule cells and neurons: CBLN1-4 are synaptic organizers expressed in cerebellum and brain
Hepatocytes: MBL2, COLEC10, COLEC11 are liver-secreted lectins
Erythroblasts/liver: ERFE (erythroferrone) is expressed in erythroblasts
cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Connective tissue / mesenchyme: broad collagen expression suggests fibroblastic or stromal origin
Cartilage: COL2A1, COL9A1-3, COL10A1, COL11A1/2 strongly indicate chondrocyte or cartilage tissue
Adipose tissue: ADIPOQ and C1QTNF family point to adipose stromal or adipocyte compartment
Lung: SFTPA1, SFTPA2, SFTPD are highly specific to pulmonary alveolar epithelium
Brain/cerebellum: CBLN1-4 and C1QL1-4 suggest neural tissue origin
Liver: MBL2, COLEC10, COLEC11 are hepatocyte-secreted acute-phase lectins
Bone marrow/erythroid: ERFE expression in erythroblasts
cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: Chondrosarcoma or osteosarcoma: overexpression of cartilage collagens (COL2A1, COL9A1, COL10A1, COL11A1)
Desmoplastic/fibrotic tumors (e.g., pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, breast cancer stroma): high COL1A1, COL3A1, COL5A1 in cancer-associated fibroblasts
Liposarcoma or adipose-derived tumors: ADIPOQ, C1QTNF members
Lung adenocarcinoma: SFTPA1/2, SFTPD may mark differentiated lung adenocarcinoma with surfactant features
Glioma or medulloblastoma: CBLN and C1QL family members in neural tumors
Macrophage-rich tumor microenvironment: C1QA/B/C high in tumor-associated macrophages
cell_malignancy_status_prediction_releva: C1QA/B/C high expression is a known marker of tumor-associated macrophages (non-malignant infiltrating immune cells), not cancer cells themselves
High fibrillar collagen expression (COL1A1, COL3A1) typically marks cancer-associated fibroblasts (non-malignant stromal cells) rather than malignant epithelial cells
ADIPOQ and C1QTNF family in adipocytes suggest non-malignant adipose stroma
SFTPA1/2/SFTPD in lung adenocarcinoma can mark well-differentiated malignant cells with retained surfactant program
COL10A1 upregulation can occur in malignant chondrocytes or hypertrophic cancer stroma
Overall, this cluster is more informative for non-malignant stromal/immune cell identification than for direct malignancy calling
drug_sensitivity_relevance: Collagen-rich ECM (COL1A1, COL3A1, COL4A1) contributes to tumor stiffness and drug penetration barriers; anti-fibrotic agents (e.g., pirfenidone, LOXL2 inhibitors) may modulate response
C1Q-expressing tumor-associated macrophages are associated with immunosuppressive microenvironments; anti-CSF1R or anti-CD47 therapies may be relevant
ADIPOQ signaling through AMPK pathway may influence sensitivity to metabolic drugs (metformin, mTOR inhibitors)
MBL2 and collectins (COLEC10/11) modulate complement-dependent cytotoxicity relevant to antibody-based therapies
CBLN/C1QL synaptic organizers may be relevant in neural tumor contexts for receptor-targeted therapies
ERFE-mediated hepcidin suppression could affect iron metabolism and sensitivity to ferroptosis-inducing agents
perturbation_modeling_relevance: Collagen genes (COL1A1, COL4A1) are relevant targets for modeling fibrosis and ECM remodeling perturbations in stromal contexts
C1QA/B/C knockdown models macrophage complement function and phagocytosis perturbations
ADIPOQ perturbation is relevant for modeling adipokine signaling and metabolic reprogramming
CBLN1-4 and C1QL1-4 perturbations are relevant for synapse formation and neural circuit modeling
SFTPA1/2/SFTPD perturbations model alveolar surfactant biology and lung injury responses
The structural homology across the cluster means co-perturbation experiments should account for potential functional redundancy within subfamilies (e.g., C1QTNF members)
qc_warnings: The cluster conflates multiple biologically distinct cell types (macrophages, chondrocytes, adipocytes, lung epithelium, neurons, fibroblasts) under a single structural superfamily criterion, which may reduce utility for cell-type-specific analyses
Clustering appears driven by sequence/structural homology (C1q globular domain + collagen triple helix) rather than co-expression or shared pathway membership in a single cell type
CD70 (a TNF superfamily member, not a C1q-domain protein) appears potentially misassigned or included due to naming similarity
C1QTNF3-AMACR is a read-through fusion transcript and its inclusion may reflect annotation artifact
COLQ (collagen-like tail of acetylcholinesterase) and OTOL1 (otolin-1) are functionally distant from fibrillar collagens despite structural similarity
Mixed lineage signals (immune, stromal, neural, epithelial) suggest this cluster would not cleanly separate cell types in single-cell analyses and may require sub-clustering
clusters.rationale: The 66 genes in this cluster share the C1q globular domain and/or collagen triple-helix structural motifs, reflecting a superfamily-level grouping rather than a functionally coherent pathway or cell-type-specific co-expression module. The collagen genes span fibrillar (COL1, COL2, COL3, COL5, COL11), network-forming (COL4), FACIT (COL9, COL16, COL21, COL22), and other non-fibrillar types. The C1q-domain proteins include complement (C1QA/B/C), adipokines (ADIPOQ, C1QTNF1-9), synaptic organizers (CBLN1-4, C1QL1-4), collectins (MBL2, COLEC10/11, SFTPA1/2/D), and others (COLQ, ERFE, GLDN, OTOL1). This structural superfamily clustering is biologically valid at the evolutionary/structural level but creates a mixed-lineage cluster that spans fibroblasts, chondrocytes, adipocytes, macrophages, pneumocytes, and neurons. The representative gene COL9A1 is a cartilage-specific FACIT collagen, consistent with the collagen component. Clustering plausibility is partially coherent: structurally justified but functionally heterogeneous.
recommended_followups: Sub-cluster the C1q-domain proteins separately from the collagen genes to obtain functionally purer modules
Verify CD70 inclusion—it is a TNF superfamily member and may be a clustering artifact
Examine co-expression evidence (e.g., from GTEx or single-cell atlases) to determine whether these genes are truly co-expressed in any single cell type or tissue
Assess whether C1QTNF3-AMACR fusion transcript should be excluded as an annotation artifact

For single-cell applications, split into at least: (a) fibrillar collagens/fibroblast module, (b) cartilage collagen module, (c) C1q complement/macrophage module, (d) adipokine/C1QTNF module, (e) surfactant/collectin module, (f) synaptic C1q module
Test enrichment of this cluster against known ECM and matrisome gene sets to confirm structural basis of clustering

clusters.title: Large Heterogeneous Cluster: Cell Cycle, Transcription, RNA Processing, Metabolism, and Spermatogenesis
clusters.overall_function: This very large cluster (1860 genes) encompasses a broad and heterogeneous set of biological functions including cell cycle regulation, transcription and RNA processing, ubiquitin-proteasome system, mitochondrial function, lipid metabolism, sialylation/glycosylation, DNA repair, autophagy, immune signaling, and spermatogenesis-related programs. The sheer size and functional diversity suggest this may be a catch-all or residual cluster from a co-expression or co-regulation analysis, possibly reflecting broadly co-regulated housekeeping and stress-response genes mixed with tissue-specific programs.
cell_type_relevance: Proliferating cells: MKI67, MCM2, POLE, BUB1B, MAD2L1, CENPA, NDC80, TTK suggest active cell cycle/mitosis

qc_warnings: Cluster is extremely large (1860 genes), suggesting possible over-merging or failure to resolve distinct biological programs
Highly heterogeneous: contains testis-specific, neural, erythroid, immune, and broadly expressed housekeeping genes in the same cluster
Presence of many SMIM (small integral membrane) genes, NPIP family, FAM genes, and uncharacterized ORFs suggests possible technical or low-information gene grouping

clusters.rationale: The representative gene GBF1 (Golgi-specific brefeldin A resistance factor 1) is a Golgi trafficking regulator, but the cluster as a whole does not cohere around any single pathway. The presence of MTRNR2L pseudogenes is a known single-cell RNA-seq quality control concern. Sub-clustering is strongly recommended.
recommended_followups: Sub-cluster this large cluster using higher resolution or alternative algorithms to resolve biologically coherent sub-modules

Perform pathway enrichment analysis on sub-clusters to identify coherent biological programs
Assess whether spermatogenesis, neural, erythroid, and immune gene sets form distinct sub-clusters

clusters.title: Histone H2A/H2B Family and Chromatin Regulatory Factors
clusters.overall_function: This cluster is dominated by core histone H2A and H2B family members (canonical and variant), along with chromatin assembly factor CHRAC1, histone variant macroH2A1, H2AZ1/2, H2AX, and transcription-related factors NFYB and multiple TAF11L paralogs. H2AX expression is relevant to DNA damage response states and may mark cells under genotoxic stress
H2AZ1/H2AZ2 and macroH2A1 are variant histones associated with gene regulation and senescence/differentiation states
NFYB involvement suggests transcriptionally active cell states

MacroH2A1 has known roles in hepatocyte differentiation and liver biology
H2AZ variants are enriched in embryonic and stem cell contexts
No strong tissue-specific signature; cluster likely reflects a proliferative/chromatin-state signature rather than a specific tissue
cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: Upregulation of replication-dependent histones is a hallmark of rapidly proliferating cancer cells across many tumor types
H2AX (gamma-H2AX) is a canonical marker of DNA double-strand breaks and genomic instability in cancer

TAF11L paralogs may reflect transcriptional amplification programs in cancer

Overall, this cluster is more likely to mark malignant or proliferating cells than resting non-malignant cells
drug_sensitivity_relevance: Histone deacetylase inhibitors (HDACi) and bromodomain inhibitors (BETi) modulate H2A/H2B-associated chromatin states and may show differential sensitivity in cells with high histone expression

MacroH2A1 perturbation models could inform differentiation and senescence programs

qc_warnings: The cluster contains a large number of histone gene paralogs (H2AC and H2BC families) which are highly co-expressed due to replication coupling and may co-cluster artifactually based on expression correlation rather than functional specificity

clusters.rationale: The cluster is overwhelmingly composed of H2A and H2B histone family members (both canonical replication-dependent and variant forms), which naturally co-cluster due to shared expression patterns in proliferating cells and shared chromatin functions. CHRAC1 is a known chromatin accessibility complex subunit. H2AX, H2AZ1/2, and macroH2A1 are well-characterized histone variants with distinct regulatory roles. NFYB is a transcription factor subunit. The TAF11L paralogs are a recently expanded gene family of uncertain function. LINC02218 is an outlier. The core histone content is highly coherent; the peripheral members (TAF11L family, LINC02218) reduce overall coherence and may represent co-expression noise.
recommended_followups: Verify whether TAF11L paralogs show correlated expression with H2A/H2B genes in single-cell RNA-seq data or whether their clustering is driven by genomic proximity

clusters.title: Serine Protease Superfamily: Kallikreins, Granzymes, Elastases, and Related Proteases
clusters.overall_function: This cluster comprises a broad collection of serine proteases spanning multiple subfamilies: tissue kallikreins (KLK1-15), granzymes (GZMA/B/H/K/M), neutrophil/mast cell proteases (ELANE, PRTN3, AZU1, CTSG, CMA1, TPSAB1/B2/D1/G1), pancreatic/digestive serine proteases (PRSS1/2/3, CELA1/2A/2B/3A/3B, CTRB1/2, CTRC, CTRL), and numerous testis/tissue-enriched PRSS family members. The unifying biochemical feature is the chymotrypsin-fold serine protease catalytic mechanism (Ser-His-Asp triad). Functions span extracellular matrix remodeling, immune cytotoxicity, inflammation, digestion, and tissue homeostasis.
cell_type_relevance: Cytotoxic T lymphocytes and NK cells: GZMA, GZMB, GZMH, GZMK, GZMM are canonical markers of cytotoxic lymphocyte identity and activation
Neutrophils: ELANE, PRTN3, AZU1, CTSG are hallmark azurophil granule proteases of neutrophils
Mast cells: TPSAB1, TPSB2, TPSD1, TPSG1, CMA1 are defining markers of mast cell subtypes (tryptase/chymase)
Pancreatic acinar cells: PRSS1, PRSS2, PRSS3, CTRB1, CTRB2, CELA family members are acinar cell digestive enzymes
Prostate epithelium: KLK3 (PSA), KLK2, KLK4 are highly prostate-specific
Epididymis/testis: PRSS21, PRSS37, PRSS41, PRSS48, PRSS50, PRSS51, TMPRSS12, TMPRSS9 are enriched in male reproductive tract
cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Prostate gland: KLK3, KLK2, KLK4, KLK15 are among the most prostate-enriched genes known
Pancreas (exocrine/acinar): PRSS1/2/3, CELA, CTRB, CTRC, CTRL are diagnostic of pancreatic acinar origin
Neutrophil/myeloid lineage: ELANE, PRTN3, AZU1, CTSG, PRSS33, PRSS57 mark granulocyte differentiation
Mast cell tissue compartment: tryptase/chymase genes (TPSAB1, TPSB2, CMA1) indicate mast cell-rich tissues (lung, gut, skin)
Cytotoxic lymphocyte compartment: granzyme expression marks T/NK cell-rich tissues or tumors with immune infiltration
Skin/brain/kidney: KLK5, KLK6, KLK7, KLK8 have tissue-specific expression in these compartments
cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: Prostate cancer: KLK3 (PSA) is the canonical prostate cancer biomarker; KLK2, KLK4, KLK11, KLK14 are also elevated in prostate adenocarcinoma
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: PRSS1/2/3, CELA, CTRB expression may indicate acinar-to-ductal metaplasia or acinar cell carcinoma
Ovarian/breast cancer: multiple KLKs (KLK5, KLK6, KLK7, KLK10, KLK11) have been associated with gynecological malignancies
Lung/colorectal cancer: KLK6, KLK10 have reported upregulation in these cancers
Immune cell tumors: granzyme expression in tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes or NK/T-cell lymphomas
cell_malignancy_status_prediction_releva: KLK3 and related kallikreins are strongly associated with malignant prostate epithelium vs. normal; high KLK expression may indicate malignant transformation
Granzyme-expressing cells (GZMA/B) in a tumor context are more likely non-malignant cytotoxic immune infiltrates, suggesting non-malignant status for those cells
Neutrophil protease genes (ELANE, PRTN3, AZU1) in a tumor context likely represent non-malignant tumor-associated neutrophils
Mast cell tryptase/chymase genes mark non-malignant stromal mast cells in tumor microenvironment
Elevated PRSS1/2/3 in non-pancreatic tumors may indicate malignant reprogramming or acinar differentiation
drug_sensitivity_relevance: KLK3 (PSA) is used clinically to monitor response to androgen deprivation therapy and enzalutamide/abiraterone in prostate cancer; KLK2/KLK4 may similarly reflect AR pathway activity
Granzyme B (GZMB) expression in tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes is a biomarker of response to immune checkpoint inhibitors (anti-PD1/PD-L1)
ELANE and PRTN3 are targets in neutrophil-mediated inflammatory contexts; sivelestat (ELANE inhibitor) is clinically used
Mast cell tryptase (TPSAB1/TPSB2) inhibitors are in development for allergic and inflammatory diseases
PRSS1 mutations and activity are relevant to pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer drug contexts
Serine protease inhibitors (serpins, small molecules) broadly relevant to this cluster
perturbation_modeling_relevance: KLK3 promoter is androgen-responsive; AR pathway perturbations (e.g., DHT treatment, enzalutamide) would strongly modulate KLK2/3/4 expression - useful as readout genes in AR perturbation models
GZMB/GZMA perturbation in cytotoxic T cells affects killing capacity; relevant for CAR-T and immunotherapy perturbation modeling
ELANE/PRTN3 knockouts in neutrophil differentiation models affect granule formation and inflammatory signaling
Granzyme network has complex redundancy; GI (genetic interaction) screens in cytotoxic lymphocytes could reveal epistasis among GZMA/B/H/K/M
PRSS1 gain-of-function mutations are a model for hereditary pancreatitis; relevant for organoid perturbation models
KLK cascade perturbations relevant to skin barrier function modeling (KLK5/7/14 in desquamation)
qc_warnings: The cluster merges functionally and cell-type-distinct serine proteases: cytotoxic lymphocyte granzymes, neutrophil granule proteases, mast cell proteases, pancreatic digestive enzymes, and prostate/reproductive kallikreins are co-clustered purely on sequence/structural homology rather than shared biological context

This likely reflects sequence-similarity-based clustering (chymotrypsin fold) rather than co-expression or pathway co-membership, which may limit biological interpretability in single-cell or expression-based analyses

Several PRSS genes (PRSS37, PRSS38, PRSS41, PRSS45P, PRSS48, PRSS50, PRSS51, PRSS53, PRSS54, PRSS55, PRSS58) are poorly characterized and testis-enriched; their inclusion may reflect sequence homology clustering artifacts
PRSS45P is annotated as a pseudogene - its presence warrants QC attention
Mixed lineage signals (immune vs. epithelial vs. exocrine) make this cluster unsuitable as a single cell-type marker set without sub-clustering
If used in expression-based analysis, co-expression of granzymes with KLKs or pancreatic proteases in the same cell would be biologically implausible and should trigger doublet/contamination checks
clusters.rationale: All 64 members belong to the chymotrypsin-clan serine protease superfamily, unified by the catalytic Ser-His-Asp triad and trypsin/chymotrypsin fold. The cluster is coherent at the protein family level but spans multiple distinct biological contexts: (1) KLK1-15 are tissue kallikreins with roles in prostate biology, skin desquamation, and cancer biomarkers; (2) GZMA/B/H/K/M are cytotoxic granule proteases of T/NK cells; (3) ELANE, PRTN3, AZU1, CTSG are neutrophil azurophil granule proteases; (4) TPSAB1/B2/TPSD1/TPSG1/CMA1 are mast cell tryptases/chymases; (5) PRSS1/2/3, CELA, CTRB, CTRC, CTRL are pancreatic digestive enzymes; (6) numerous PRSS family members are testis/epididymis-enriched. The representative gene KLK3 (PSA) is the canonical prostate cancer biomarker. Clustering is plausible at the sequence/structural level but biologically heterogeneous for expression-based applications.
recommended_followups: Sub-cluster this group by expression pattern (co-expression networks) to separate immune, epithelial, and exocrine protease modules
Verify PRSS45P pseudogene status and consider removal from expression analyses
Use granzyme sub-cluster (GZMA/B/H/K/M) as a cytotoxic lymphocyte signature independently
Use KLK2/3/4 as a prostate epithelial/cancer signature independently
Check for doublets in single-cell data if multiple protease subtypes (e.g., granzymes + KLKs) co-express in the same cell
Perform GO enrichment and tissue expression atlas cross-referencing to validate sub-cluster tissue specificity
Assess whether PRSS family testis genes cluster separately in expression space from immune and digestive proteases

clusters.title: Intermediate Filament Cytoskeletal Proteins – Keratin-Dominated Structural Network
clusters.overall_function: This cluster is dominated by intermediate filament (IF) proteins, with a large representation of keratin family members (type I and type II keratins, hair keratins) alongside non-keratin IFs including desmin (DES), vimentin (VIM), peripherin (PRPH), internexin neuronal intermediate filament alpha (INA), neurofilament light (NEFL), lamins (LMNA, LMNB1, LMNB2), and the lens-associated BFSP2. Together these proteins form the structural cytoskeletal scaffold of epithelial, mesenchymal, neuronal, and muscle cells, maintaining cell shape, mechanical integrity, and nuclear architecture.
cell_type_relevance: Basal epithelial cells (KRT5/KRT14 co-expression is a canonical basal keratinocyte marker)
Suprabasal/differentiated keratinocytes (KRT1/KRT10, KRT2)
Simple epithelial cells (KRT8/KRT18/KRT19)
Hair follicle and hair shaft cells (KRT31-KRT40, KRT71-KRT86 hair keratins)
Mesenchymal/fibroblast-like cells undergoing EMT (VIM)
Muscle cells (DES)
Peripheral neurons (PRPH, INA, NEFL)
Lens fiber cells (BFSP2)
Cycling or stressed epithelial cells (KRT16/KRT17 wound-response keratins)
cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Skin/epidermis: broad keratin repertoire including basal (KRT5/14), suprabasal (KRT1/10), and palmoplantar (KRT9) markers strongly indicates epidermal origin
Hair follicle/appendage: extensive hair keratin representation (KRT31-40, KRT71-86)
Corneal epithelium: KRT12/KRT3 are cornea-specific markers
Gastrointestinal/simple epithelium: KRT8/KRT18/KRT19/KRT20 mark luminal epithelial lineages
Peripheral nervous system: PRPH, INA, NEFL suggest neuronal tissue contribution

cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: Squamous cell carcinoma: KRT5/KRT14/KRT6A/KRT6B/KRT16/KRT17 are hallmarks of squamous differentiation programs
Basal-like breast cancer: KRT5/KRT14/KRT17 mark basal-like subtype
Luminal breast cancer: KRT8/KRT18/KRT19 mark luminal epithelial identity
Colorectal/gastric adenocarcinoma: KRT20/KRT8/KRT18 mark intestinal-type carcinomas

Sarcoma/EMT state: VIM upregulation marks mesenchymal cancer states
Neuroblastoma/peripheral nerve sheath tumors: PRPH/NEFL/INA may mark neuronal differentiation
cell_malignancy_status_prediction_releva: Keratin expression patterns can distinguish malignant epithelial cells from stromal/immune non-malignant cells, supporting malignancy calling in carcinomas
VIM co-expression with keratins may indicate partial EMT in malignant cells
KRT16/KRT17 upregulation is associated with wound-response and stress programs that can be elevated in malignant epithelial cells
Loss of differentiation-associated keratins (KRT1/KRT10) may indicate dedifferentiation in malignant keratinocytes
Lamin (LMNA/LMNB1/LMNB2) expression changes are associated with nuclear envelope alterations in cancer
drug_sensitivity_relevance: KRT14/KRT5 basal identity may predict resistance to luminal-targeting therapies in breast cancer
VIM-high EMT state is associated with resistance to EGFR inhibitors and chemotherapy
KRT17 expression has been linked to mTOR pathway activity and may predict sensitivity to mTOR inhibitors
Desmin (DES) mutations affect cytoskeletal integrity relevant to cardiotoxicity of anthracyclines in muscle
Lamin alterations (LMNA) affect nuclear mechanics and may modulate sensitivity to DNA-damaging agents
perturbation_modeling_relevance: Keratins are structural proteins with complex redundancy; perturbation of individual keratins (e.g., KRT14 KO) models epidermolysis bullosa-like phenotypes
VIM knockout is a classical EMT perturbation model affecting cell migration and invasion
LMNA perturbation models laminopathy and nuclear stiffness changes relevant to mechanobiology
DES perturbation models desminopathy in muscle differentiation contexts
This cluster is highly relevant for modeling epithelial differentiation trajectories and EMT transitions in GEARS/perturbation frameworks
Hair keratin knockouts model hair shaft structural defects and follicle biology
qc_warnings: The cluster is functionally coherent at the broad level of intermediate filament proteins but spans multiple distinct cell lineages (epithelial, neuronal, muscle, lens) that would not co-express all members in any single cell type

Mixing of epithelial keratins with neuronal IFs (NEFL, INA, PRPH), muscle IF (DES), and lens IF (BFSP2) suggests the clustering algorithm grouped by sequence/structural homology or co-regulation at the gene family level rather than cell-type-specific co-expression
BFSP2 (lens-specific beaded filament) is an outlier and may represent a false positive or overly broad IF grouping
Lamins (LMNA, LMNB1, LMNB2) are ubiquitously expressed nuclear envelope proteins and could represent housekeeping contamination
The 61-member cluster is large; sub-clustering by keratin type (type I vs type II vs hair vs simple epithelial) and by non-keratin IF class would improve biological resolution
No obvious batch or stress artifact, but the breadth of lineages warrants caution in single-cell co-expression interpretation
clusters.rationale: The cluster is anchored by a comprehensive set of keratin genes spanning type I (KRT9-KRT28, KRT31-KRT40) and type II (KRT1-KRT8, KRT71-KRT86) families, consistent with a gene-family-level grouping of intermediate filament proteins. The representative gene KRT14 is a canonical basal epithelial marker. Non-keratin IFs (VIM, DES, PRPH, INA, NEFL, BFSP2) and nuclear lamins (LMNA, LMNB1, LMNB2) are included, reflecting the broader IF superfamily. While all members share the IF structural domain, their cell-type expression patterns are highly divergent, making this cluster most useful for identifying epithelial identity and differentiation state in carcinoma contexts, with caveats about lineage mixing.
recommended_followups: Sub-cluster the 61 members by expression correlation in a reference single-cell atlas to separate epithelial, neuronal, muscle, and lens IF modules

clusters.title: Immunoglobulin Heavy Chain Variable (IGHV) Gene Segments
clusters.overall_function: This cluster comprises immunoglobulin heavy chain variable (IGHV) gene segments spanning multiple subfamilies (IGHV1 through IGHV8), including functional genes, pseudogenes, and orphon loci (IGHV1OR, IGHV2OR, IGHV3OR). These segments encode the variable domain of the immunoglobulin heavy chain, which forms the antigen-binding site of antibodies. They undergo V(D)J recombination in B cells to generate antibody diversity.
cell_type_relevance: B cells at all developmental stages (pro-B, pre-B, immature B, naive B, memory B, plasma cells) — IGHV expression marks B-lineage identity
Plasma cells and plasmablasts — high-level immunoglobulin expression
Germinal center B cells — IGHV genes subject to somatic hypermutation
Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) cells — IGHV mutation status is a key prognostic marker
Memory B cells — carry somatically hypermutated IGHV sequences
cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Strong predictor of B-cell lineage origin; expression of IGHV genes is essentially restricted to B lymphocytes and their progeny
Bone marrow (B-cell development) and secondary lymphoid organs (germinal centers, spleen, lymph nodes)
Peripheral blood B cells
Mucosal-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT)
cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: B-cell malignancies: CLL/SLL — IGHV mutation status (mutated vs. unmutated) is a major prognostic biomarker
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) — IGHV usage and mutation patterns inform clonal origin
Follicular lymphoma — clonal IGHV rearrangements define tumor clones
Multiple myeloma / plasma cell myeloma — clonal IGHV rearrangements present
Mantle cell lymphoma, marginal zone lymphoma, Burkitt lymphoma — all carry clonal IGHV rearrangements
Specific IGHV genes (e.g., IGHV3-21, IGHV1-69) are enriched in certain B-cell malignancy subtypes
cell_malignancy_status_prediction_releva: IGHV expression alone does not distinguish malignant from non-malignant B cells; clonal restriction (single IGHV rearrangement dominating) is the key malignancy indicator
In single-cell RNA-seq, detection of a single dominant IGHV transcript across many cells suggests clonal expansion consistent with malignancy
Polyclonal IGHV expression across cells is consistent with normal B-cell populations
IGHV mutation status (somatic hypermutation load) can help distinguish germinal-center-experienced (memory/GC) from naive B cells
drug_sensitivity_relevance: IGHV mutation status in CLL predicts response to chemoimmunotherapy (mutated IGHV associated with better response to FCR regimen)
Unmutated IGHV in CLL associated with BCR signaling dependency, predicting sensitivity to BTK inhibitors (ibrutinib, acalabrutinib) and PI3K-delta inhibitors (idelalisib)
Specific IGHV genes (e.g., IGHV3-21) in CLL may confer distinct signaling properties affecting drug response
Anti-CD20 therapies (rituximab, obinutuzumab) target B cells broadly regardless of IGHV usage
perturbation_modeling_relevance: IGHV genes are not typical perturbation targets (they are germline-encoded and rearranged); however, their expression levels can serve as readouts of B-cell differentiation state in perturbation screens
In CRISPR screens targeting B-cell differentiation regulators, IGHV expression changes can serve as downstream phenotypic markers
BCR signaling pathway perturbations (e.g., BTK, SYK, PI3K knockouts) would be expected to alter IGHV-expressing cell survival/proliferation
IGHV pseudogenes and orphons (IGHV1OR, IGHV3OR) are unlikely to be expressed and may represent noise in perturbation readouts
qc_warnings: Cluster includes IGHV orphon loci (IGHV1OR15-1, IGHV1OR15-9, IGHV1OR21-1, IGHV2OR16-5, IGHV3OR15-7, IGHV3OR16-* series, IGHV4OR15-8, IGHV5-10-1 possibly) — these are located outside the main IGH locus and may not be expressed; their inclusion may reflect sequence homology-based co-clustering rather than functional co-expression
Some IGHV genes listed are pseudogenes (e.g., IGHV3-35, IGHV3-38, IGHV7-81) — if detected in RNA-seq, could represent mapping artifacts or read-through transcription

High co-expression of many IGHV genes in a single cell is unusual (only one productive rearrangement per B cell); bulk-level co-expression clustering is expected, but single-cell co-detection of multiple IGHV genes may indicate multi-mapping or ambient RNA contamination
IGHV8-51-1 is a non-human primate-like orphon; its presence warrants verification of genome annotation version used
clusters.rationale: All 61 entities are members of the IGHV gene family, encoding the variable regions of immunoglobulin heavy chains. The cluster spans all major IGHV subfamilies (IGHV1-IGHV7, plus orphon IGHV1OR/IGHV2OR/IGHV3OR/IGHV4OR groups). This is a highly coherent cluster from a gene family perspective — these genes share structural homology, genomic organization within the IGH locus (or related orphon loci), and functional role in antibody variable domain encoding. Their co-clustering likely reflects shared sequence features and co-expression in B-lineage cells. The inclusion of orphon and pseudogene members is a minor concern but does not undermine the overall coherence. The cluster is highly informative for B-cell identity, clonality assessment, and B-cell malignancy characterization.
recommended_followups: Verify which IGHV members are functional vs. pseudogenes vs. orphons using IMGT database annotation to filter noise
In single-cell data, assess whether individual cells express one or multiple IGHV genes to distinguish productive rearrangements from multi-mapping artifacts
Use clonality analysis (single dominant IGHV + CDR3) to distinguish malignant from polyclonal normal B cells
Correlate IGHV mutation status (somatic hypermutation) with clinical annotations if CLL or other B-cell malignancy data is present
Check for ambient RNA contamination if IGHV transcripts appear in non-B-cell clusters

clusters.title: Cytochrome P450 Superfamily and Sulfotransferase Drug/Steroid Metabolism Cluster
clusters.overall_function: This cluster is dominated by cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes spanning multiple subfamilies involved in xenobiotic metabolism, steroidogenesis, bile acid synthesis, vitamin D/retinoic acid metabolism, and fatty acid hydroxylation, complemented by sulfotransferase (SULT) enzymes that conjugate and inactivate steroids, xenobiotics, and other small molecules. Together these genes represent the core phase I and phase II biotransformation machinery.
cell_type_relevance: Hepatocytes (primary site of CYP2C/2D/3A/1A2 and SULT expression)
Adrenocortical cells (CYP11A1, CYP17A1, CYP21A2 steroidogenic enzymes)
Granulosa/theca cells and placental syncytiotrophoblasts (CYP19A1 aromatase)
Intestinal epithelial cells (CYP3A4, CYP3A5, SULT1A1)
Lung epithelial cells (CYP1A1, CYP1B1, CYP2F1, CYP4B1)
Renal proximal tubule cells (CYP27B1, CYP24A1 vitamin D metabolism)
cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Strong liver signature: CYP3A4, CYP2D6, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP1A2, CYP2E1, CYP7A1, CYP8B1, SULT2A1 are highly liver-enriched
Adrenal cortex: CYP11A1, CYP17A1, CYP21A2 steroidogenic enzymes are adrenal markers
Ovary/testis/placenta: CYP19A1 (aromatase) marks steroidogenic gonadal/placental tissue
Kidney: CYP27B1, CYP24A1 suggest renal tubular contribution
Skin/retinal pigment epithelium: CYP4V2, CYP26 family members
Lung: CYP2F1, CYP4B1, CYP1A1 suggest airway epithelial contribution
cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC): high CYP3A4, CYP2C9, CYP1A2, CYP7A1 expression is characteristic of well-differentiated HCC
Adrenocortical carcinoma: CYP11A1, CYP17A1, CYP21A2 steroidogenic program
Breast/ovarian cancer: CYP19A1 (aromatase) activity relevant to estrogen-driven tumors
Cholangiocarcinoma: bile acid synthesis enzymes CYP7A1, CYP8B1
Lung adenocarcinoma: CYP1A1, CYP1B1, CYP2F1 expression
Endometrial cancer: SULT1E1, CYP1B1 estrogen metabolism genes
cell_malignancy_status_prediction_releva: High expression of this cluster generally marks well-differentiated, non-malignant or low-grade hepatocytes; loss of CYP expression is a hallmark of hepatocyte dedifferentiation in HCC
In adrenal tumors, retained steroidogenic CYP expression may indicate functional adenoma vs. carcinoma
CYP1B1 is paradoxically upregulated in many cancers and could mark malignant cells
SULT downregulation relative to CYP upregulation may indicate altered phase II capacity in malignant cells
Overall, high cluster activity more consistent with non-malignant or well-differentiated states in liver; context-dependent in other tissues
drug_sensitivity_relevance: CYP3A4, CYP2D6, CYP2C9, CYP2C19 are the major drug-metabolizing enzymes determining pharmacokinetics of >70% of clinical drugs; expression levels predict drug clearance and toxicity
CYP2C9 variants affect warfarin, NSAIDs sensitivity
CYP19A1 (aromatase) is the direct target of aromatase inhibitors (letrozole, anastrozole, exemestane) in breast cancer
CYP17A1 is the target of abiraterone in prostate cancer
CYP24A1 upregulation confers resistance to vitamin D-based therapies
CYP1B1 activates certain pro-carcinogens and prodrugs
SULT1A1 activity affects tamoxifen activation (4-hydroxytamoxifen sulfation)
CYP2E1 mediates acetaminophen hepatotoxicity
perturbation_modeling_relevance: This cluster is highly relevant for modeling CYP enzyme perturbations affecting drug metabolism (e.g., CYP3A4 knockout effects on drug clearance)
Steroidogenesis pathway perturbations (CYP11A1, CYP17A1, CYP21A2) model congenital adrenal hyperplasia or adrenal insufficiency
CYP19A1 perturbation models estrogen biosynthesis disruption
CYP26 family knockouts model retinoic acid signaling dysregulation
SULT perturbations affect sulfation capacity and hormone inactivation
Genetic interaction modeling between CYP and SULT genes could reveal compensatory phase I/II balance mechanisms
Relevant for GEARS-style multi-gene perturbation prediction in hepatocyte or steroidogenic cell contexts
qc_warnings: The cluster mixes hepatic drug-metabolizing CYPs with steroidogenic CYPs and retinoic acid/vitamin D CYPs, which have distinct tissue expression patterns; functional coherence is at the superfamily level rather than a single pathway
CYP3A7-CYP3A51P is a pseudogene/read-through transcript and may introduce noise
CYP2D7 is a pseudogene and its inclusion warrants QC attention for potential mapping artifacts
CYP2A7 is also a pseudogene; presence of multiple pseudogenes suggests possible cross-mapping or annotation issues
TBXAS1 (thromboxane synthase) is a CYP superfamily member but functionally distinct (platelet/eicosanoid biology); its inclusion is structurally justified but biologically divergent
The cluster is very large (60 genes) and may benefit from sub-clustering to separate hepatic xenobiotic, steroidogenic, and lipid/vitamin metabolism modules
clusters.rationale: All 60 entities are either cytochrome P450 (CYP) family members or sulfotransferases (SULT), making this one of the most coherent superfamily-level clusters possible. CYP enzymes share the heme-containing monooxygenase fold and catalyze oxidative metabolism of endogenous substrates (steroids, bile acids, vitamins) and xenobiotics. SULTs perform conjugation reactions that typically inactivate or solubilize CYP products. The co-clustering of CYPs and SULTs reflects their coordinated phase I/II metabolic roles. Pseudogene entries (CYP2D7, CYP2A7, CYP3A7-CYP3A51P) are a minor QC concern. TBXAS1 is a legitimate CYP superfamily member. The cluster is biologically coherent at the superfamily level with expected tissue heterogeneity across liver, adrenal, gonad, lung, and kidney.
recommended_followups: Sub-cluster analysis to separate hepatic xenobiotic CYPs (CYP3A4, CYP2D6, CYP2C9, CYP1A2), steroidogenic CYPs (CYP11A1, CYP17A1, CYP19A1, CYP21A2), and vitamin/lipid CYPs (CYP24A1, CYP26A1/B1/C1, CYP27B1, CYP4 family)
Pseudogene QC: verify that CYP2D7, CYP2A7, and CYP3A7-CYP3A51P reads are not cross-mapping artifacts from their functional paralogs
