Assess co-expression with nuclear receptors (PXR/NR1I2, CAR/NR1I3, AhR) that transcriptionally regulate this cluster
Evaluate SULT/CYP ratio as a potential biomarker of phase I/II balance in malignant vs. non-malignant hepatocytes

clusters.title: Basic Helix-Loop-Helix (bHLH) Transcription Factor Network: Neurogenesis, Myogenesis, and Lineage Specification
clusters.overall_function: This cluster comprises a comprehensive set of basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) transcription factors spanning multiple subfamilies: proneural activators (NEUROG1/2/3, NEUROD1/2/4/6, ASCL1-5, ATOH1/7), myogenic regulatory factors (MYOD1, MYF5, MYF6, MYOG), HES/HEY Notch effector repressors (HES1-7, HEY1/2, HEYL), ID dominant-negative inhibitors (ID1-4), and lineage-specifying bHLH factors for mesoderm, cardiac, and other tissues (HAND1/2, MESP1, MSGN1, TWIST1/2, TAL1/2, SCX, TCF15/21/23/24, FIGLA, MSC, BHLHE22/23). Together they form the core transcriptional regulatory network governing cell fate decisions across neural, muscle, cardiac, and other developmental lineages.
cell_type_relevance: Neural progenitor cells and neuroblasts (NEUROG1/2, ASCL1, NEUROD1/2/4/6)
Myoblasts and skeletal muscle progenitors (MYOD1, MYF5, MYF6, MYOG)
Cardiac progenitors and cardiomyocytes (HAND1, HAND2, MESP1)
Notch-active progenitor/stem cell states with active Notch signaling (HES1, HES5, HEY1/2)
Quiescent or inhibited progenitors (ID1-4 high states)
Intestinal secretory progenitors (ATOH1/ASCL2)
Pancreatic endocrine progenitors (NEUROG3, NEUROD1)
Mesenchymal/EMT-like states (TWIST1/2)
Hematopoietic progenitors (TAL1/TAL2)
Cerebellar granule neuron progenitors (ATOH1)
cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Neural tissue: strong proneural bHLH signature (NEUROG1/2/3, ASCL1, NEUROD family) points to brain, spinal cord, peripheral nervous system
Skeletal muscle: MRF quartet (MYOD1, MYF5, MYF6, MYOG) is definitive for skeletal muscle lineage
Cardiac/mesoderm: HAND1/2, MESP1, MSGN1, TCF15 indicate cardiac or paraxial mesoderm origin
Pancreas: NEUROG3 and NEUROD1 are hallmarks of pancreatic endocrine tissue
Intestinal epithelium: ATOH1 and ASCL2 mark intestinal secretory and stem cell compartments
Retina: ATOH7 is specific to retinal ganglion cell progenitors
Hematopoietic system: TAL1/TAL2 indicate blood/endothelial progenitor context
cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC): ASCL1 and NEUROD1 are master regulators of SCLC subtypes; this cluster could classify SCLC molecular subtypes
Neuroblastoma: ASCL1, HAND2, PHOX2 pathway adjacency; NEUROD1 marks adrenergic neuroblastoma state
Medulloblastoma: ATOH1 is a key driver of SHH-subgroup medulloblastoma
Rhabdomyosarcoma: MYOD1, MYF5, MYOG are diagnostic markers of rhabdomyosarcoma
Glioma/glioblastoma: ASCL1, OLIG3, ID1-4 relate to glioma stem cell and proneural GBM states
Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors: NEUROG3, NEUROD1 are relevant
Leukemia/lymphoma: TAL1 is an oncogene in T-ALL; ID proteins are relevant in B-cell malignancies
Breast cancer: TWIST1/2 drive EMT and metastatic programs; ID1 marks cancer stem cells
cell_malignancy_status_prediction_releva: ID1-4 overexpression is associated with malignant, dedifferentiated, and stem-like cancer states; high ID expression may mark malignant cells
ASCL1 and NEUROD1 expression can distinguish malignant neuroendocrine cancer cells from normal tissue
TWIST1/2 upregulation is a hallmark of EMT-driven malignancy and metastatic potential
HES1 overexpression in Notch-active tumors may mark malignant progenitor-like states
Conversely, terminal differentiation bHLH factors (MYOG, NEUROD6) may mark more differentiated, less malignant states
The balance of activator vs. repressor bHLH factors (e.g., ASCL1 vs. HES1, activators vs. ID proteins) could serve as a malignancy index
drug_sensitivity_relevance: ASCL1-high SCLC is associated with sensitivity to DLL3-targeting therapies (rovalpituzumab) and aurora kinase inhibitors
NEUROD1-high SCLC subtype shows differential sensitivity to chemotherapy regimens
MYOD1-mutant rhabdomyosarcoma may have altered sensitivity to targeted agents
Notch pathway inhibitors (gamma-secretase inhibitors) would be predicted to affect HES/HEY expression and downstream bHLH balance
ID protein inhibition (e.g., via BMP pathway modulation) is an emerging therapeutic concept in cancer stem cells
TWIST1/2-driven EMT programs confer resistance to conventional chemotherapy; targeting TWIST may restore sensitivity
TAL1 in T-ALL is associated with sensitivity to specific targeted therapies in that context
perturbation_modeling_relevance: This cluster is highly relevant for perturbation modeling of transcription factor networks: bHLH factors form a well-characterized activator-repressor hierarchy ideal for GI (genetic interaction) mapping
ASCL1 vs. NEUROD1 perturbations in SCLC models are paradigmatic for lineage plasticity studies
MYOD1 overexpression is a classic transdifferentiation perturbation benchmark
HES1 knockdown/knockout in Notch perturbation experiments is well-established
ID1-4 perturbations model stem cell vs. differentiation state transitions
NEUROG2/NEUROG1 overexpression drives neuronal transdifferentiation, relevant for GEARS-like forward prediction of cell state changes
The activator/repressor bHLH balance makes this cluster ideal for modeling epistatic interactions in AIVC frameworks
HAND1/HAND2 perturbations are relevant for cardiac differentiation modeling from iPSCs
qc_warnings: The cluster spans multiple developmental lineages (neural, muscle, cardiac, hematopoietic) which may reflect the shared bHLH domain rather than a single biological process; functional coherence is at the protein family level rather than a single pathway
ID proteins (ID1-4) are antagonists/inhibitors of the other bHLH factors in this cluster; their co-clustering reflects structural/domain similarity but opposite functional roles

MXD1/MXD3/MXD4/MXI1 are MYC-antagonizing bHLH-LZ proteins that may have been included due to bHLH domain similarity; their primary function (MYC network repression) is somewhat distinct from developmental bHLH programs
TCFL5 and TFEC are less characterized members; their inclusion should be verified
No obvious housekeeping gene contamination detected
Cluster appears to be a curated bHLH transcription factor family cluster, which is biologically valid but functionally heterogeneous
clusters.rationale: All 60 genes encode proteins containing a basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) domain, the defining structural feature of this transcription factor superfamily. The cluster can be subdivided into: (1) Class II tissue-specific bHLH activators for neural (NEUROG1/2/3, NEUROD1/2/4/6, ASCL1-5, ATOH1/7, NHLH1/2, OLIG3), muscle (MYOD1, MYF5, MYF6, MYOG, MSC), cardiac/mesoderm (HAND1/2, MESP1, MSGN1, TCF15/21/23/24, SCX), and other lineages (FIGLA, BHLHE22/23, FERD3L, BHLHA9/15, TAL1/2, TWIST1/2, TFEC, TCFL5); (2) Class I/IV inhibitory HES/HEY Notch effectors (HES1-7, HEY1/2, HEYL); (3) ID dominant-negative inhibitors (ID1-4); (4) MXD/MXI MYC-antagonizing factors (MXD1/3/4, MXI1). The clustering is driven by shared bHLH domain sequence similarity and co-regulatory roles in developmental cell fate decisions. The representative gene NEUROG1 is a canonical proneural bHLH factor. This cluster is highly informative for cell type classification in neural, muscle, and cardiac contexts, and for cancer subtype classification in SCLC, neuroblastoma, medulloblastoma, and rhabdomyosarcoma.
recommended_followups: Subdivide cluster into functional sub-clusters: proneural, myogenic, cardiac, HES/HEY repressors, ID inhibitors, MXD/MXI repressors for more granular analysis
Validate cluster coherence using protein-protein interaction networks (STRING/BioGRID) to confirm known bHLH dimerization partners are co-clustered
Apply cluster to SCLC single-cell datasets to test ASCL1 vs. NEUROD1 subtype classification
Test cluster gene set enrichment in neuroblastoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, and medulloblastoma bulk RNA-seq datasets

Investigate whether HES/HEY vs. proneural bHLH ratio can serve as a Notch activity readout in tumor microenvironment analyses

clusters.title: Defensins and WFDC-domain Antimicrobial Peptide Cluster
clusters.overall_function: Innate immune defense via antimicrobial peptides (AMPs): alpha-defensins, beta-defensins, and WFDC/WAP-domain protease inhibitors. These small cysteine-rich peptides disrupt microbial membranes, modulate inflammation, and inhibit serine proteases, collectively forming a first-line mucosal and epithelial barrier against pathogens.
cell_type_relevance: Neutrophils (alpha-defensins DEFA1/3/4 are major granule components)
Paneth cells (DEFA5/6 are hallmark Paneth cell markers in small intestinal crypts)
Mucosal epithelial cells (beta-defensins expressed in skin, airway, gut epithelium)
Epididymal epithelium (EPPIN, WFDC genes highly expressed in male reproductive tract)
Innate immune cells broadly (neutrophils, macrophages, dendritic cells)
cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Small intestine / ileum (DEFA5, DEFA6 are Paneth cell-specific markers)
Neutrophil-rich tissues or bone marrow (DEFA1, DEFA3, DEFA4)
Skin and mucosal epithelia (DEFB1, DEFB4A, DEFB103A)
Male reproductive tract / epididymis (EPPIN, WFDC10A/B, WFDC11, WFDC13)
Lung / airway epithelium (SLPI, WFDC2 expressed in respiratory mucosa)
Cervix and female reproductive tract (WFDC2/HE4 expressed in gynecological tissues)
cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: Ovarian cancer / endometrial cancer: WFDC2 (HE4) is a well-established ovarian cancer biomarker; high expression may indicate gynecological malignancy
Colorectal or intestinal cancer: DEFA5/6 expression can mark intestinal differentiation programs
Lung adenocarcinoma: SLPI and WFDC2 are expressed in lung cancer subtypes
Prostate cancer: EPPIN and related WFDC genes may reflect prostate/epididymal lineage programs
cell_malignancy_status_prediction_releva: WFDC2 (HE4) overexpression is strongly associated with malignant ovarian and endometrial tumors; its presence may help distinguish malignant from benign epithelial cells
SLPI and PI3 (elafin) can be upregulated in malignant epithelial contexts but are also expressed in normal mucosa, limiting specificity
Alpha-defensins (DEFA1/3) in tumor microenvironment may reflect neutrophil infiltration rather than intrinsic malignancy
Overall, this cluster is more informative for tissue/lineage identity than binary malignancy status, with WFDC2 as the strongest malignancy-associated member
drug_sensitivity_relevance: SLPI and PI3 (elafin) inhibit serine proteases (elastase, trypsin); tumors with high expression may show altered sensitivity to protease-dependent drug activation or resistance to neutrophil elastase-mediated cytotoxicity
WFDC2 (HE4) expression correlates with platinum resistance in ovarian cancer; high cluster activity may predict reduced chemosensitivity
Defensin-mediated membrane disruption mechanisms are relevant to understanding resistance to membrane-targeting agents
SLPI has anti-inflammatory roles that may modulate immunotherapy response
perturbation_modeling_relevance: Paneth cell differentiation models: DEFA5/6 are key readouts for intestinal organoid Paneth cell specification perturbations
Neutrophil differentiation: DEFA1/3/4 knockouts or overexpression would model granule biogenesis
WFDC2 perturbation relevant to modeling ovarian cancer drug resistance programs
Beta-defensin locus (chromosome 8p23 gene cluster) is a copy-number variable region; CNV perturbations affect multiple DEFB genes simultaneously, complicating single-gene perturbation models
SLPI/PI3 perturbations relevant to modeling mucosal inflammation and protease-antiprotease balance
qc_warnings: Many DEFB genes are paralogs in tandem arrays on chromosome 8p23 and 20p13; co-clustering may partly reflect sequence homology rather than independent co-regulation

Several gene pairs are likely read-through transcripts or near-identical paralogs (DEFA1/DEFA1B, DEFB103A/DEFB103B, DEFB104A/DEFB104B, DEFB130A/DEFB130B, etc.); these may not represent truly independent expression signals
EPPIN-WFDC6 is a read-through fusion gene; its presence alongside both EPPIN and WFDC6 as separate entries may inflate apparent cluster size

Alpha-defensins (neutrophil granule) and Paneth cell defensins (DEFA5/6) have distinct cell-type expression patterns; their co-clustering may reflect shared AMP function rather than co-expression in a single cell type
WFDC2 (HE4) is a cancer biomarker with broad expression; its inclusion with highly tissue-restricted defensins warrants scrutiny
clusters.rationale: The cluster is dominated by alpha-defensins (DEFA1-6), beta-defensins (DEFB1, DEFB4A/B, DEFB103A-DEFB136), and WFDC/WAP-domain proteins (WFDC2-13, SLPI, PI3, EPPIN). All share roles in innate immunity as antimicrobial peptides or serine protease inhibitors with cysteine-rich structural motifs. The clustering is biologically coherent at the functional level (AMP/innate defense), though the mixture of neutrophil-specific alpha-defensins, Paneth cell defensins, epithelial beta-defensins, and reproductive tract WFDC proteins suggests the cluster captures a broad AMP gene family rather than a single cell-type co-expression module. The high proportion of paralogous gene pairs and read-through transcripts is a notable QC concern. WFDC2 stands out as a clinically important cancer biomarker. Confidence is moderate-high for functional annotation but lower for single-cell-type specificity.
recommended_followups: Examine single-cell RNA-seq co-expression to determine whether alpha-defensins and beta-defensins truly co-express or represent distinct cell-type modules that were merged
Check for copy-number variation artifacts: DEFB gene cluster on 8p23 is highly CNV-prone and may introduce technical co-variation
Separate WFDC2 from the defensin core and assess whether its clustering is driven by functional similarity or co-expression in specific tissues (e.g., fallopian tube, lung)
Validate paralog pairs (DEFA1/DEFA1B, DEFB103A/DEFB103B) for redundancy and consider collapsing for downstream analyses
Assess whether EPPIN-WFDC6 read-through transcript should be treated as a distinct entity or merged with its component genes

clusters.title: Antigen Presentation & Immune Recognition: MHC-I/II, Immunoglobulins, TCR Constant Regions, and NKG2D Ligands
clusters.overall_function: This cluster encompasses the core machinery of adaptive and innate immune recognition: classical and non-classical MHC class I molecules (HLA-A/B/C/E/F/G), MHC class II molecules (HLA-DR/DQ/DP/DM/DO), CD1 lipid antigen-presenting molecules, immunoglobulin constant region genes (IgG/A/M/D/E, kappa/lambda light chains), T-cell receptor constant regions (alpha/beta/gamma/delta), NKG2D stress ligands (MICA/MICB, ULBP1-3, RAET1E/G/L), and accessory molecules (B2M, FCGRT, HFE, MR1, PROCR, AZGP1). Together these genes define antigen presentation, adaptive immune effector identity, and innate immune surveillance.
cell_type_relevance: Professional antigen-presenting cells (dendritic cells, macrophages, B cells) — high MHC-II expression
Cytotoxic T lymphocytes and NK cells — NKG2D ligand upregulation marks stressed/transformed targets
B cells and plasma cells — immunoglobulin constant region expression (IGHG1-4, IGHA1/2, IGHM, IGKC, IGLC1-3/7)
T cells — TCR constant region genes (TRBC1/2, TRDC, TRGC1/2) mark αβ and γδ T cell populations
NKT and MAIT cells — CD1 family and MR1 expression
Trophoblasts and immune-privileged cells — non-classical HLA-E/F/G expression
Stressed or transformed cells upregulating NKG2D ligands (MICA/MICB, ULBPs)
cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Lymphoid tissues (lymph node, spleen, thymus) — rich in all adaptive immune cell types expressing these genes
Bone marrow — B cell and plasma cell immunoglobulin expression
Peripheral blood — mixed immune cell populations
Gut-associated lymphoid tissue — IgA-expressing plasma cells (IGHA1/2), γδ T cells
Liver — FCGRT (neonatal Fc receptor), HFE (hemochromatosis protein), AZGP1 expression
Placenta/trophoblast — HLA-G, HLA-E non-classical expression
cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: B cell lymphomas and multiple myeloma — immunoglobulin constant region overexpression
T cell lymphomas — TCR constant region expression
Antigen presentation loss in tumor cells — downregulation of HLA-A/B/C and B2M is a hallmark of immune evasion
Stress-induced NKG2D ligand upregulation (MICA/MICB, ULBPs) marks transformed or genomically unstable cancer cells
Hepatocellular carcinoma — AZGP1, HFE, FCGRT context
Cervical/endometrial cancers — HLA-G upregulation as immune evasion marker
cell_malignancy_status_prediction_releva: Loss of classical MHC-I (HLA-A/B/C, B2M) expression is a strong indicator of malignant immune evasion
Upregulation of NKG2D ligands (MICA/MICB, ULBP1-3, RAET1E/G/L) suggests cellular stress or malignant transformation
Non-classical HLA-G/E upregulation in non-trophoblast contexts suggests malignant immune privilege
High immunoglobulin expression distinguishes B cell malignancies from non-malignant B cells by clonality patterns
TCR constant region expression helps distinguish T cell malignancies from reactive T cell infiltrates
drug_sensitivity_relevance: Anti-PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint immunotherapy response correlates with MHC-I expression levels (HLA-A/B/C, B2M integrity)
FCGRT expression influences IgG half-life and pharmacokinetics of therapeutic antibodies
HFE mutations affect iron metabolism and may modulate sensitivity to iron-dependent therapies
NKG2D ligand upregulation predicts sensitivity to NK cell-based therapies and NKG2D-targeting bispecifics
CD1-restricted lipid antigen presentation relevant to NKT cell-activating immunotherapies
MICA/MICB shedding is a resistance mechanism to NK cell therapies; anti-MICA antibodies are in development
MHC-II expression on tumor cells correlates with response to immune checkpoint blockade
perturbation_modeling_relevance: B2M knockout is a canonical model for MHC-I loss and immune evasion — highly relevant for CRISPR perturbation screens
HLA locus perturbations are complex due to high polymorphism but relevant for antigen presentation modeling
MICA/MICB knockdown models NK cell evasion mechanisms
CD1 family perturbations model lipid antigen presentation pathways
Immunoglobulin constant region genes are relevant for modeling B cell differentiation and plasma cell identity
TCR constant region perturbations model T cell identity and signaling
FCGRT perturbation models antibody recycling and therapeutic antibody pharmacokinetics
NKG2D ligand panel (ULBP1-3, RAET1E/G/L) perturbations model innate immune stress response
qc_warnings: Cluster mixes functionally distinct immune gene families: MHC-I, MHC-II, CD1, immunoglobulins, TCR constant regions, and NKG2D ligands — these are co-expressed in different cell types and may reflect a broad 'immune gene' co-expression module rather than a single pathway

Immunoglobulin constant region genes (IGHG1-4, IGHA1/2, IGHM, IGKC, IGLC1-3/7) are primarily expressed in B cells/plasma cells, while TCR constant regions (TRBC1/2, TRDC, TRGC1/2) are T cell-specific — their co-clustering may indicate immune cell contamination in a non-immune dataset or a pan-immune signature

AZGP1 and PROCR are somewhat unexpected in this cluster; AZGP1 is a zinc-binding glycoprotein expressed in secretory epithelia, and PROCR (endothelial protein C receptor) is primarily endothelial — these may represent noise or indirect co-regulation
HLA-DOB is a non-classical MHC-II molecule with restricted expression; its clustering with broadly expressed MHC-II genes warrants attention

Cluster may be driven by genomic co-localization (MHC locus on chr6p21) for HLA genes, but immunoglobulin and TCR genes are on different chromosomes — co-expression rather than genomic proximity likely drives clustering
In single-cell data, this cluster could reflect doublets or mixed immune cell populations
clusters.rationale: The cluster is anchored by HLA-B and contains a comprehensive set of immune recognition molecules. The MHC-I (HLA-A/B/C/E/F/G) and MHC-II (HLA-DR/DQ/DP/DM/DO) genes form a coherent antigen presentation core. CD1 family members extend this to lipid antigen presentation. NKG2D ligands (MICA/MICB, ULBP1-3, RAET1E/G/L) represent innate immune stress sensing. B2M, FCGRT, HFE, and MR1 are accessory molecules functionally linked to antigen presentation. The immunoglobulin constant regions and TCR constant regions are less expected co-members but could reflect co-regulation in immune-rich tissues or datasets. AZGP1 and PROCR are outliers. Overall the cluster captures a broad immune recognition gene program, likely derived from a dataset with significant immune cell content or from analysis of immune-related gene expression programs.
recommended_followups: Assess whether immunoglobulin and TCR constant region genes form a separable sub-cluster from MHC/antigen-presentation genes using higher-resolution clustering
Check for doublet contamination in single-cell data — co-expression of B cell (Ig) and T cell (TCR) markers in the same cells is suspicious
Investigate AZGP1 and PROCR expression patterns to determine if they are genuine co-regulated members or noise
Perform cell-type deconvolution to determine which cell types drive this cluster's expression
Examine MHC-I expression loss (HLA-A/B/C, B2M) as a malignancy/immune evasion biomarker in the dataset
Test NKG2D ligand expression as a stress/transformation marker across cell states in the dataset
Validate HLA-G/E expression patterns for immune privilege signatures in non-trophoblast cells

clusters.title: Olfactory Receptor Gene Cluster (OR51/OR52/OR56 Family)
clusters.overall_function: This cluster comprises a large set of olfactory receptor (OR) genes belonging to subfamilies OR51, OR52, and OR56. These are G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) involved in odorant detection in the olfactory epithelium. They signal through Golf/cAMP pathways to mediate the sense of smell. Some members (e.g., OR51E2) have documented ectopic expression in non-olfactory tissues including prostate and other cancers.
cell_type_relevance: Olfactory sensory neurons (primary canonical cell type expressing these receptors)
Olfactory epithelial sustentacular or basal cells (minor expression)
Ectopic expression in prostate luminal epithelial cells (OR51E2 is a known prostate marker)
Possible low-level expression in gut enteroendocrine cells for some OR members
cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Strong signal for olfactory epithelium / nasal mucosa origin
OR51E2 (PSGR) is a well-known marker of prostate tissue, suggesting possible prostate epithelial origin if OR51E2 is highly expressed

Cluster composition spanning OR51/OR52/OR56 subfamilies is consistent with a chromosomal locus on 11q (human OR gene cluster region), pointing to olfactory tissue or a tissue with ectopic OR expression
cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: OR51E2 (also known as PSGR) is overexpressed in prostate cancer and may serve as a prostate cancer marker
Some ORs have been reported ectopically expressed in breast, colon, and lung cancers, though functional significance is largely unclear
Cluster could mark prostate adenocarcinoma cells if OR51E2 expression is dominant
Ectopic OR expression in cancer may reflect epigenetic deregulation rather than a specific cancer cell state
cell_malignancy_status_prediction_releva: OR51E2 upregulation is associated with malignant prostate epithelium, potentially distinguishing malignant from benign prostate cells
Broad OR gene expression across many family members may indicate olfactory neuroblastoma (esthesioneuroblastoma) or other neuroendocrine tumors

drug_sensitivity_relevance: OR51E2 has been explored as a therapeutic target in prostate cancer; agonists may inhibit prostate cancer cell proliferation via cAMP-dependent mechanisms
GPCR-targeting strategies (small molecule agonists/antagonists) could be relevant for OR51E2-expressing tumors
No established drug sensitivity associations for the majority of OR52/OR56 members

CRISPR knockout of individual OR genes is feasible but functional readouts in non-olfactory contexts are unclear

These genes are unlikely to be strong hits in standard cancer perturbation screens due to low expression in most cell lines
qc_warnings: OR51C1P and OR56B2P are pseudogenes (indicated by 'P' suffix) and should be flagged; their inclusion may reflect genomic co-localization rather than functional expression

The cluster spans three OR subfamilies (OR51, OR52, OR56) which are genomically proximal on chromosome 11q but may not be co-expressed in all tissues — clustering may reflect genomic linkage rather than co-expression
If this cluster was derived from expression data, high OR gene co-expression could be an artifact of olfactory tissue contamination or batch effects
Pseudogene inclusion (OR51C1P, OR56B2P) warrants QC review of the input data
clusters.rationale: All 55 entities are olfactory receptor genes from the OR51, OR52, and OR56 subfamilies, which are well-established members of the large human OR gene superfamily. These genes are genomically clustered on chromosome 11q and encode GPCRs canonically expressed in olfactory sensory neurons. The cluster is highly coherent from a gene family perspective. OR51E2 (PSGR) is a notable outlier with documented ectopic expression and functional roles in prostate cancer. Two pseudogenes (OR51C1P, OR56B2P) are present. The clustering is biologically plausible as a genomic/family-based grouping, though functional co-expression in non-olfactory tissues should be verified.
recommended_followups: Verify whether clustering was based on sequence similarity, genomic proximity, or expression co-variation — this affects interpretation
Check expression levels of OR51E2 specifically across samples to assess prostate cancer relevance
Remove or flag pseudogenes (OR51C1P, OR56B2P) before downstream functional analysis
Assess whether OR gene expression in the dataset derives from olfactory tissue samples or represents ectopic expression
Investigate chromosomal co-localization on 11q11-q12 to confirm genomic clustering as a potential confound

clusters.title: Ciliary/Flagellar Axoneme and Sperm Tail Structural Components
clusters.overall_function: This cluster is enriched for genes encoding structural and regulatory components of cilia and flagella, particularly sperm flagellar axoneme assembly, outer dense fiber organization, and ciliary motility. Members include outer dense fiber proteins (ODF3, ODF3B, ODF3L1, ODF3L2), cilia and flagella associated proteins (CFAP126, CFAP77), sperm-associated antigens (SPAG8), testis-expressed genes (TEX26, TEX36, TEX37, TEX45), and multiple uncharacterized ORFs likely involved in ciliary/flagellar biogenesis. The cluster likely represents a co-regulated transcriptional program active in ciliated and spermatogenic cells.
cell_type_relevance: Spermatocytes and spermatids undergoing flagellogenesis
Ciliated epithelial cells (e.g., airway, ependymal, fallopian tube)
Multi-ciliated cells expressing motile cilia programs
Testicular germ cells at late spermatogenic stages
cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Testis (primary): high expression of TEX genes, ODF family, and SPAG8 strongly suggests testicular germ cell origin
Respiratory epithelium: CFAP genes and PIFO are associated with motile cilia in airway cells
Brain ependymal cells: motile cilia markers such as STPG1/2 and CCSAP are expressed in ependymal lining
Fallopian tube epithelium: ciliated cells share flagellar gene programs
cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: Testicular germ cell tumors (TGCTs): TEX and ODF gene expression may mark seminoma or non-seminoma subtypes
Lung adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma with aberrant ciliogenesis programs
Ovarian cancer subtypes with ciliated cell-of-origin signatures
Cancer-testis antigen programs: several TEX genes may be re-expressed in diverse cancers as cancer-testis antigens
cell_malignancy_status_prediction_releva: Non-malignant spermatogenic or ciliated cells are the primary expected source of this signature

Low or absent expression in most somatic non-ciliated malignant cells would suggest non-malignant ciliated cell identity

drug_sensitivity_relevance: Taxane sensitivity: microtubule-associated proteins (MAP6D1, SAXO1, CCSAP) may modulate tubulin stability and taxane response
Ciliary pathway inhibitors: disruption of flagellar/ciliary assembly genes could sensitize cells to agents targeting cilia-dependent signaling (e.g., Hedgehog pathway inhibitors)
Cancer-testis antigen immunotherapy: TEX gene products may serve as tumor-specific antigens for vaccine or T-cell therapy approaches
Limited direct drug target relevance for most members given structural/scaffolding roles
perturbation_modeling_relevance: Perturbation of ODF or CFAP genes would be informative for modeling flagellar assembly checkpoints
PIFO and STPG family knockouts could model primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD)-like states
TEX gene perturbations relevant for modeling spermatogenesis failure or male infertility programs
Co-perturbation of multiple cluster members could reveal epistatic relationships in axoneme assembly
CCSAP and SAXO1 perturbations relevant for microtubule stabilization studies in ciliated contexts
qc_warnings: High proportion of uncharacterized ORFs (C*orf genes) may reduce functional annotation confidence
NEB and NEBL (nebulin family, sarcomeric proteins) are outliers with primary roles in muscle sarcomere organization rather than cilia/flagella — possible contamination or co-regulation artifact
NRAP (nebulin-related anchoring protein) is also muscle-associated and may represent a clustering artifact
ATP6V1FNB is a vacuolar ATPase subunit with broad expression, potentially a housekeeping contaminant
MDM1 function is less clearly ciliary and may represent noise
clusters.rationale: The cluster is dominated by well-established ciliary and flagellar genes: ODF3 family members are canonical outer dense fiber proteins of sperm flagella; CFAP126 and CFAP77 are cilia and flagella associated proteins; SPAG8 is a sperm-associated antigen; TEX26/36/37/45 are testis-expressed genes consistent with spermatogenesis; PIFO, STPG1/2/4, CCSAP, SAXO1, and MAP6D1 are associated with cilia/flagella structure or microtubule regulation. The many uncharacterized C*orf genes likely represent novel ciliary components identified through co-expression. The cluster is largely coherent but contains a few outliers (NEB, NEBL, NRAP, ATP6V1FNB, MDM1) that may reflect co-regulation artifacts or noise. clusters.title: Extracellular Matrix, Cell Surface Receptor & Secreted Protein Landscape
clusters.overall_function: This cluster encompasses the broad extracellular and cell-surface proteome: ECM structural proteins (collagens, laminins, fibronectin, proteoglycans), secreted enzymes and their inhibitors (MMPs, ADAMs, ADAMTS, cathepsins, serine proteases, TIMPs), cell adhesion molecules (integrins, cadherins, IgSF members, selectins, nectins), growth factor receptors and ligands (EGF family, FGF, TGF-β, Wnt/FZD, Notch, Eph/ephrin, PDGF, IGF), complement and coagulation cascade components, glycosylation and glycan-remodeling enzymes (GALNTs, CHSTs, B3/B4 transferases, sulfatases), immune checkpoint and co-stimulatory molecules (CD274/PD-L1, TIGIT, BTLA, ICOS, CD28, TLRs, SIGLECs, SLAMFs), and a wide array of secreted signaling modulators. Together these genes define the extracellular communication layer of the cell.

qc_warnings: Extremely large cluster (1769 genes) suggesting over-aggregation or a very broad functional category rather than a tight biological module
Mixed lineage contamination: cluster contains markers of many distinct cell types (hepatocytes, neurons, immune cells, epithelial, endothelial, fibroblasts) simultaneously
Likely driven by shared feature of secreted/transmembrane topology rather than a single coherent pathway or cell type
Testis/sperm-specific genes (ADAM2/7/18/20/21/29/30/32, CRISP1-3, ZP2-4, ZPBP2, IZUMO1R) mixed with broadly expressed ECM genes - possible annotation-level clustering artifact
Neuronal synaptic genes (NRXN1-3, NLGN2-4, GRIA1-4, GRIK1-5, GRM1-8) co-clustered with immune and ECM genes - biologically distinct programs
Housekeeping secretory pathway genes (CALR, CANX, LMAN1, TMED family, OS9, PRKCSH) included alongside tissue-specific secreted proteins
Complement and coagulation factors (liver-specific) mixed with immune cell surface markers - may reflect shared signal peptide/secretion rather than co-expression
Cluster may represent a 'secretome/surfaceome' annotation cluster rather than a co-expression or co-regulation cluster
clusters.rationale: The 1769 genes in this cluster share the common property of encoding secreted, extracellular, or single-pass/multi-pass transmembrane proteins that function at the cell surface or in the extracellular space. The representative gene ITGB4 is a cell adhesion integrin, consistent with this theme. The cluster encompasses: (1) ECM structural and remodeling proteins (collagens, laminins, fibronectin, proteoglycans, MMPs, ADAMs, ADAMTS, TIMPs, LOXLs); (2) cell surface receptors across many families (RTKs, cytokine receptors, GPCRs, integrins, IgSF, TNFR, TLRs); (3) secreted signaling molecules (growth factors, complement, coagulation factors, acute-phase proteins); (4) glycosylation enzymes (GALNTs, CHSTs, B3/B4GTs, sulfatases, mannosidases); (5) immune surface molecules (CD antigens, checkpoint molecules, SIGLECs, SLAMFs). The biological coherence is at the level of subcellular localization (extracellular/membrane) rather than a single pathway or cell type. This is a common outcome when clustering is performed on features that capture secretory signal or transmembrane topology. The cluster is useful as a 'surfaceome/secretome' reference but should be sub-clustered for more specific biological inference.
recommended_followups: Sub-cluster this large cluster using stricter co-expression or pathway-based criteria to identify tighter functional modules (e.g., ECM remodeling, complement, synaptic, immune checkpoint sub-clusters)
Assess whether clustering was driven by GO annotation similarity (secreted/membrane) rather than actual co-expression - compare with expression correlation matrices
Perform enrichment analysis per sub-group: hepatocyte secretome, neuronal synaptic, immune surface, ECM structural, glycosylation enzyme sub-clusters
Use cell-type deconvolution to determine which genes in this cluster are co-expressed in the same cell type vs. expressed in distinct cell types
Validate ITGB4 as representative: check if ITGB4 expression correlates with other cluster members or if it is an outlier representative
Apply UMAP or hierarchical clustering within this cluster to identify biologically meaningful sub-modules for downstream perturbation or drug target analysis
Cross-reference with Human Protein Atlas secretome/membrane proteome annotations to confirm the shared topology hypothesis

clusters.title: Glutathione S-Transferases, Chloride Intracellular Channels, and Cyclophilins – Detoxification and Protein Folding Cluster
clusters.overall_function: This cluster encompasses three functionally related but distinct protein families: (1) Glutathione S-transferases (GSTA1-5, GSTM1-5, GSTZ1, HPGDS) involved in phase II detoxification, oxidative stress response, and prostaglandin synthesis; (2) Chloride intracellular channels (CLIC1-5) involved in ion transport, cell volume regulation, and apoptosis; and (3) Cyclophilins/peptidyl-prolyl isomerases (PPIA, PPIB, PPIC, PPIF, PPIH, PPIL1, PPIL3, PPIL6, PPIAL4A/C/D/E/F/G/H) involved in protein folding, chaperone activity, and spliceosome function. SH3BGRL and SH3BGRL2 are SH3 domain-binding glutaredoxin-like proteins. The cluster broadly represents cellular stress response, detoxification, and proteostasis.
cell_type_relevance: Hepatocytes and liver parenchymal cells (high GST expression)
Erythrocytes and erythroid progenitors (CLIC1, GSTM, PPIA enriched)
Epithelial cells with high detoxification capacity (intestinal, renal tubular)
Cells under oxidative or xenobiotic stress
Cycling or proliferating cells (cyclophilins support protein folding demand)
cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Liver: GSTA1/2/3/4/5 and GSTM family are classically liver-enriched detoxification enzymes
Kidney: GST and CLIC family members are expressed in renal tubular epithelium
Intestine: GST isoforms are expressed in enterocytes
Erythroid lineage: CLIC1, GSTM, and PPIA are highly expressed in red blood cells and precursors
Lung: GSTM and CLIC4 have notable expression in airway epithelium
cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: Hepatocellular carcinoma: GST overexpression is a hallmark of drug-resistant HCC
Colorectal cancer: GSTM and GSTA isoforms are frequently upregulated
Lung adenocarcinoma: GSTM1 and CLIC1 are associated with cancer cell survival
Leukemia/lymphoma: PPIA (cyclophilin A) is upregulated in hematologic malignancies

cell_malignancy_status_prediction_releva: GST family upregulation can mark malignant cells with acquired drug resistance, but GSTs are also highly expressed in normal hepatocytes and epithelial cells, limiting specificity
CLIC1 overexpression has been reported in several tumor types and may help distinguish malignant from normal epithelium in some contexts

Overall, this cluster alone is insufficient to reliably distinguish malignant from non-malignant cells without additional context
drug_sensitivity_relevance: GST overexpression (GSTA, GSTM) is a well-known mechanism of resistance to alkylating agents (e.g., chlorambucil, melphalan, busulfan) and platinum-based drugs
HPGDS-mediated prostaglandin D2 synthesis may modulate inflammatory tumor microenvironment and response to COX/HPGDS inhibitors
PPIA (cyclophilin A) is the target of cyclosporin A; cyclophilin inhibitors (e.g., alisporivir) may be relevant

SH3BGRL proteins may modulate redox signaling affecting drug response
perturbation_modeling_relevance: GST knockouts are classical models for studying xenobiotic metabolism and oxidative stress response
PPIA/cyclophilin perturbations affect protein folding, splicing (spliceosome cyclophilins PPIH, PPIL1, PPIL3), and viral replication – relevant for perturbation screens
CLIC channel perturbations affect apoptosis sensitivity and could be informative in cell death pathway screens
Co-perturbation of GST family members may reveal synthetic lethality with oxidative stress inducers

qc_warnings: The cluster mixes three distinct protein families (GSTs, CLICs, cyclophilins) with different primary functions; co-clustering may reflect shared stress-response or housekeeping co-expression rather than a single coherent pathway
PPIAL4A/C/D/E/F/G/H are highly similar paralogs; their co-clustering may reflect sequence similarity artifacts or co-expression due to gene family expansion rather than functional specificity
NKTR (NK-tumor recognition protein / IL-2 conjugate precursor) appears functionally discordant with the rest of the cluster and may represent a clustering artifact or annotation ambiguity
SH3BGRL and SH3BGRL2 are loosely related to glutaredoxin/thioredoxin biology but their inclusion with GSTs and cyclophilins warrants scrutiny

clusters.rationale: The cluster contains three recognizable protein families: GSTs (alpha, mu, zeta, and hematopoietic prostaglandin D synthase subfamilies) involved in detoxification and oxidative stress; CLICs (1-5) involved in chloride transport and apoptosis; and cyclophilins (PPIA, PPIB, PPIC, PPIF, PPIH, PPIL1, PPIL3, PPIL6, and PPIAL4 paralogs) involved in protein folding and splicing. These families share a broad association with cellular stress response and proteostasis, which may explain their co-clustering in expression data. However, the mechanistic connections are indirect. NKTR is an outlier. The PPIAL4 paralog expansion may introduce noise. The cluster is most informative for liver/epithelial tissue of origin and drug resistance contexts (GSTs), with secondary relevance for protein folding perturbation studies (cyclophilins).
recommended_followups: Investigate whether NKTR co-expression with this cluster is consistent across datasets or represents a batch/annotation artifact
Assess whether PPIAL4 paralogs can be collapsed or treated as a single functional unit for downstream analyses
Perform pathway enrichment (e.g., Reactome, KEGG) to determine whether a unifying stress-response or detoxification pathway links all three families
Validate GST cluster expression in liver and intestinal single-cell datasets to confirm tissue-of-origin signal
Test whether this cluster's expression correlates with chemotherapy resistance phenotypes in cancer cell line databases (e.g., CCLE, GDSC)

clusters.title: SERPIN Superfamily: Serine Protease Inhibitors
clusters.overall_function: This cluster comprises members of the SERPIN (serine protease inhibitor) superfamily, a large family of structurally related protease inhibitors that regulate diverse biological processes including coagulation, fibrinolysis, inflammation, complement activation, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Members include both secreted (clade A) and intracellular (clade B) serpins, as well as those involved in hormone transport (SERPINA7), angiogenesis (SERPINF1), and collagen folding (SERPINH1).
cell_type_relevance: Hepatocytes: many clade A serpins (SERPINA1, SERPINA3, SERPINC1, SERPIND1, AGT) are predominantly liver-synthesized acute-phase proteins

cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Liver: high expression of SERPINA1, SERPINA3, SERPINC1, SERPIND1, SERPINA6, SERPINA7, AGT strongly suggests hepatocyte or liver origin

qc_warnings: The cluster spans multiple SERPIN clades (A, B, C, D, E, F, H, I) with distinct tissue distributions and functions; while all are structurally related serpins, functional coherence is based on shared structural fold rather than shared pathway or co-expression
AGT (angiotensinogen) is a serpin family member but primarily functions as a hormone precursor rather than a protease inhibitor; its inclusion is structurally justified but functionally divergent
SERPINF1 (PEDF) is primarily an anti-angiogenic and neurotrophic factor, diverging from classical protease inhibitor function
Mixing of secreted (clade A) and intracellular (clade B) serpins may reflect sequence/structural clustering rather than co-expression or co-regulation in any single cell type
Cluster likely derived from sequence homology-based grouping; biological interpretation should account for clade-specific functions
clusters.rationale: All 34 entities are members of the SERPIN superfamily, identifiable by the SERPIN prefix nomenclature. The cluster is highly coherent at the structural/family level, grouping all major human SERPIN clades. Clade A serpins (SERPINA1-12) are predominantly liver-secreted acute-phase proteins regulating coagulation and inflammation. Clade B serpins (SERPINB1-13) are largely intracellular and expressed in epithelial and immune cells. Other clades include coagulation regulators (SERPINC1/antithrombin, SERPIND1/heparin cofactor II), fibrinolysis regulators (SERPINE1/PAI-1, SERPINF2/alpha-2-antiplasmin), and specialized members (SERPINH1/HSP47 collagen chaperone, SERPINF1/PEDF). AGT is included as a structural serpin homolog. The clustering is plausible as a gene family cluster but users should be aware that functional heterogeneity across clades limits single-pathway interpretation.
recommended_followups: Stratify cluster by SERPIN clade (A vs B vs other) for more refined cell-type and tissue-of-origin analysis

clusters.title: FGF Family and IL-1 Superfamily Signaling Ligands

The core biological theme is extracellular signaling via secreted or membrane-associated ligands that regulate cell proliferation, differentiation, tissue homeostasis, inflammation, and immune responses. FGFs signal through receptor tyrosine kinases (FGFRs) to control development, angiogenesis, metabolism, and tissue repair. IL-1 superfamily members are key mediators of innate immunity and inflammatory signaling.

FSCN2 (fascin actin-bundling protein 2, retinal) is also an outlier; it is an actin-bundling protein with no clear functional link to FGF or IL-1 biology

The cluster merges two large, functionally distinct gene families (FGFs and IL-1 superfamily) that share structural beta-trefoil folds but have very different receptors and biological roles; this may reflect sequence/structural similarity-based clustering rather than functional coherence

clusters.rationale: The cluster contains 20 FGF family members (nearly the entire human FGF ligand repertoire) and 10 IL-1 superfamily cytokines, plus two unrelated proteins (CFAP161, FSCN2). The FGF and IL-1 superfamily proteins share a beta-trefoil structural fold, which likely explains their co-clustering if the method used structural or sequence similarity. Functionally, FGFs are growth factors signaling through FGFRs to regulate development, metabolism, and tissue repair, while IL-1 family members are cytokines signaling through IL-1 receptor family members to regulate inflammation. The two outliers (CFAP161, FSCN2) have no clear connection to either family and represent likely noise or algorithmic artifacts. The cluster is partially coherent at the structural level but not at the functional/pathway level.
recommended_followups: Remove CFAP161 and FSCN2 and re-cluster to assess whether they represent noise

clusters.title: E2 Ubiquitin-Conjugating Enzyme Family

clusters.title: DNAJ/HSP40 Co-chaperone Family

clusters.title: Gap Junction / Connexin Family
clusters.overall_function: This cluster comprises members of the connexin (Cx) gene family, encoding gap junction proteins that form intercellular channels mediating direct cell-to-cell communication of ions, small molecules, and electrical signals. Members span the GJA, GJB, GJC, GJD, and GJE subfamilies, reflecting the full diversity of the connexin superfamily.
cell_type_relevance: Cardiomyocytes: GJA1 (Cx43) and GJA5 (Cx40) are hallmark cardiac conduction system markers

clusters.title: Membrane Transport, Lipid Metabolism, and Immune Signaling Superfamily

clusters.rationale: Cluster 5 is an exceptionally large (1310-gene) cluster with DUOX1 as representative. The dominant theme is membrane transport: over 200 SLC family members spanning virtually all SLC subfamilies, all ABC-A subfamily members, all aquaporins, all chloride channels (CLCN), and multiple other transporter families. Secondary themes include lipid metabolism (ELOVL, CERS, FADS, ALOX, SOAT, DGAT), NADPH oxidase biology (DUOX1/2, NOX1-5, NOXA1, NOXO1), TNF superfamily immune signaling (>20 TNFRSF and TNFSF members), and a large TMEM protein family. The breadth and size strongly suggest this cluster was formed by co-annotation (e.g., membrane localization, transport activity GO terms) or by a graph-based clustering algorithm that merged multiple functionally related but distinct modules. Individual sub-modules (SLC transporters, NOX oxidases, TNF signaling, ceramide synthesis) are internally coherent, but their co-clustering is suspicious. The cluster has utility for identifying membrane transport capacity, immune signaling state, and lipid metabolic programs, but should be decomposed into sub-clusters for precise biological interpretation.
recommended_followups: Sub-cluster this large cluster using stricter resolution parameters to identify coherent sub-modules (e.g., SLC transporters, NOX oxidases, TNF signaling, ceramide synthesis)

clusters.title: Histone H3 Gene Family Cluster
clusters.overall_function: Encodes histone H3 proteins (replication-dependent H3.1/H3.2 and replication-independent H3.3 variants) that form the core nucleosome octamer, packaging genomic DNA and serving as platforms for epigenetic modifications (methylation, acetylation, phosphorylation) that regulate chromatin accessibility, transcription, DNA repair, and cell identity.
cell_type_relevance: Replication-dependent H3.1/H3.2 variants (H3C genes) are highly expressed in S-phase cycling cells, making this cluster a strong marker of proliferating cell states

Replication-dependent (H3C1-H3C15, H3Y1, H3Y2) and replication-independent (H3-3A, H3-3B, H3-4, H3-5) variants are co-clustered; while functionally related, they have distinct expression patterns (cell-cycle-dependent vs constitutive), which may reduce functional resolution

clusters.rationale: All 20 entity IDs are unambiguously histone H3 family gene symbols. H3C1-H3C15, H3Y1, H3Y2 encode replication-dependent H3.1/H3.2 histones expressed during S-phase; H3-3A and H3-3B encode the replication-independent H3.3 variant; H3-4 and H3-5 encode additional H3 variants. clusters.title: Lipocalin / Small Secreted Lipid-Binding Protein Family
clusters.overall_function: This cluster is dominated by members of the lipocalin superfamily and related small secreted proteins involved in lipid transport, binding, and sequestration. Members include multiple lipocalins (LCN1, LCN2, LCN6, LCN8, LCN9, LCN10, LCN12, LCN15, LCNL1), odorant-binding proteins (OBP2A, OBP2B), apolipoprotein-related secreted proteins (APOD, APOM), complement component C8G, alpha-1-acid glycoproteins (ORM1, ORM2), AMBP (alpha-1-microglobulin/bikunin precursor), PAEP (glycodelin/progestagen-associated endometrial protein), and PTGDS (prostaglandin D2 synthase, a lipocalin). Collectively these proteins share a conserved beta-barrel fold for hydrophobic ligand binding and are predominantly secreted into body fluids (plasma, urine, seminal fluid, tears, cerebrospinal fluid, endometrial secretions).

clusters.rationale: All 19 members share membership in or close structural relationship to the lipocalin superfamily, defined by a conserved 8-stranded beta-barrel (calycin fold) that binds small hydrophobic ligands. The cluster includes: (1) canonical lipocalins (LCN1, LCN2, LCN6, LCN8-12, LCN15, LCNL1), (2) odorant-binding proteins (OBP2A/B, which are lipocalin-related), (3) PTGDS (lipocalin-type prostaglandin D synthase), (4) APOD and APOM (apolipoprotein lipocalins), (5) AMBP (contains lipocalin domain), (6) C8G (lipocalin fold in complement), (7) ORM1/ORM2 (acute-phase glycoproteins with structural similarity), and (8) PAEP (glycodelin, a lipocalin). The structural coherence is high. Functional coherence is moderate — all are secreted ligand-binding proteins but serve diverse physiological roles across liver, endometrium, brain, eye, nose, and reproductive tract. Clustering by co-expression or sequence similarity is biologically justified.

clusters.overall_function: This large cluster is dominated by mitochondrial biology (OXPHOS complexes I-V, mitoribosome subunits, TIM/TOM import machinery, mtDNA maintenance, CoQ biosynthesis, TCA cycle components) alongside extensive cytoplasmic and ER-resident metabolic enzymes spanning fatty acid oxidation, amino acid catabolism, nucleotide metabolism, redox homeostasis (glutathione/thioredoxin/peroxiredoxin systems), UDP-glucuronosyltransferases, short-chain dehydrogenases/reductases, and lipid metabolism. Secondary themes include ribosome biogenesis, ubiquitin-proteasome components, vesicle trafficking, and scattered signaling/receptor genes that may represent noise or co-regulated metabolic support functions.
cell_type_relevance: Highly metabolically active cells: hepatocytes, cardiomyocytes, skeletal muscle cells, neurons — all of which rely heavily on OXPHOS and mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation
Liver parenchymal cells suggested by UGT1A/2 family, AADAC, FMO1-5, CYP27A1, BHMT, GNMT, and other hepatic-enriched metabolic genes
Muscle cells (cardiac and skeletal) suggested by CKM, CKMT2, COX7A1, COX6A1, ACADVL
Neurons suggested by GABR subunits, GRIN1, GRM7, CRMP1, NRN1, though these may be outliers
Proliferating cells suggested by BIRC5, CCNB1/B2, RRM2, TRIP13, RFC2-4 — possible cycling subpopulation contamination or co-regulation
cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Liver: strongest signal from hepatic drug-metabolism genes (UGT1A/2B families, FMO1-5, AADAC, PON1, BHMT, GNMT, CYP27A1, GGT1/2, LIPA)
Skeletal/cardiac muscle: CKM, CKMT1A/B, CKMT2, COX7A1/A2, COX6A1/A2, ACADVL
Brain/neural tissue: GABR subunit families, GRIN1, GRM7, CRMP1, BCAT1, KYNU — though mixed with liver signal
Kidney: ACSM1/2A/2B, ACSM4/5, PHEX, NAALAD2 suggest proximal tubule contribution
Broad metabolic tissues: the OXPHOS and mitoribosome core is ubiquitous but enriched in high-energy-demand tissues
cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC): UGT, FMO, AADAC, BHMT, GNMT, GGT expression patterns are characteristic of hepatocyte-derived malignancies
Metabolically reprogrammed cancers: ETFDH, ACADVL, PDHA1, SUCLG1 activity relates to oxidative vs. glycolytic balance in cancer cells
Neuroblastoma or glioma: GABR subunits, GRIN1, GRM7, CRMP1, LMO1/3/4 are expressed in neural cancers
Prostate cancer: HSD17B3, HSD3B1/2, AKR1C1-4, AMACR are steroid metabolism enzymes highly relevant to androgen-driven prostate cancer
Colorectal/GI cancers: UGT1A family, AADAC, LIPA, LIPF suggest GI epithelial cancer relevance
cell_malignancy_status_prediction_releva: The OXPHOS/mitoribosome core (NDUFA/B/C/S, UQCR, COX, ATP5 subunits, MRPL/MRPS) is expressed in both normal and malignant cells but can distinguish metabolic states
Upregulation of BIRC5 (survivin), CCNB1/B2, RRM2, TRIP13 suggests malignant or proliferating cells
Downregulation of ETFDH, ACADVL, PDHA1 relative to glycolytic genes may indicate Warburg-shifted malignant cells
UGT/FMO/CYP expression is typically higher in normal hepatocytes than in dedifferentiated HCC, potentially marking non-malignant or well-differentiated cells
The mixed proliferation + differentiated metabolism signature makes binary malignant/non-malignant classification ambiguous for this cluster
drug_sensitivity_relevance: OXPHOS inhibitors (metformin, IACS-010759, rotenone analogs): NDUFS1/3/4/6/8, NDUFB subunits, UQCRC2 expression predicts sensitivity to Complex I/III inhibitors
UGT1A/2B family: major drug-glucuronidation enzymes; expression levels directly affect pharmacokinetics of irinotecan (UGT1A1), tamoxifen, morphine (UGT2B7), and many other drugs
FMO1-5: flavin-containing monooxygenases metabolize numerous drugs; expression affects drug clearance and toxicity
AKR1C1-4: involved in steroid and drug metabolism; AKR1C3 is a target in castration-resistant prostate cancer (indomethacin, ASP9521)
AMACR: target in prostate cancer; ABCG2 (multidrug resistance transporter) affects chemotherapy efflux
ETFDH mutations cause riboflavin-responsive multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency; ETFDH expression may predict response to riboflavin supplementation
NQO1/NQO2: activate bioreductive prodrugs (mitomycin C, EO9); expression predicts sensitivity
DPYD: rate-limiting enzyme in 5-fluorouracil catabolism; low DPYD predicts 5-FU toxicity
perturbation_modeling_relevance: OXPHOS subunit knockouts (NDUFS1, UQCRC2, COX4I1, ATP5PD) are classic mitochondrial perturbation targets with well-characterized fitness effects in cancer cell lines (DepMap)
PDHA1 and DLST knockouts model metabolic reprogramming between OXPHOS and glycolysis
TFAM, POLG-pathway genes (MGME1, PNPT1, SUPV3L1) model mtDNA maintenance perturbations
UBA1, UBE2S, RBX1, PSMD1 represent ubiquitin-proteasome perturbation nodes
DNMT3A perturbation relevant to epigenetic reprogramming models
BIRC5 (survivin) knockdown is a well-studied anti-cancer perturbation
CoQ biosynthesis genes (COQ2-9, PDSS1/2) model coenzyme Q deficiency syndromes
TIMM17A/B, TIMM23, TOMM6 model mitochondrial protein import perturbations
Gene interaction (GI) mapping: the dense OXPHOS subunit representation enables systematic buffering/synthetic lethality mapping within respiratory chain complexes
qc_warnings: Cluster is very large (1296 genes) suggesting possible over-merging of functionally distinct modules
Presence of GABR subunit family (GABRA1-6, GABRB1-3, GABRG1-3), GRIN1, GRM7 (neuronal receptors) alongside hepatic metabolic genes suggests lineage mixing or co-expression artifact
BIRC5, CCNB1/B2, RRM2, TRIP13, RFC2-4 are cell-cycle/proliferation genes that may represent a distinct co-regulated module
WNT3, WNT3A, SHH, ERBB4, FZD4 are signaling pathway genes that are functionally distant from the OXPHOS core
CRHR1, QRFPR, TRPC3/6/7, TRPM2/7/8 (GPCRs and TRP channels) are unlikely to be mechanistically co-clustered with mitochondrial metabolism
SAA1/SAA2/SAA4 (acute phase proteins) may indicate inflammatory or stress contamination

clusters.rationale: The cluster's representative gene ETFDH (electron transfer flavoprotein dehydrogenase) and the dominant gene sets — NDUFA/B/C/S subunits, UQCR subunits, COX subunits, ATP5 subunits, MRPL/MRPS ribosomal proteins, TIMM/TOMM import components, COQ biosynthesis genes, TCA cycle enzymes (PDHA1, DLST, SUCLG1, SDHC/D), and fatty acid oxidation enzymes (ACADVL, ACSL1, CPT2, ECHS1, ECI1) — strongly indicate a mitochondrial metabolism and OXPHOS core. Layered on top are extensive hepatic drug-metabolism enzymes (UGT1A/2B, FMO1-5, AKR1C1-4, AADAC, CYP27A1), redox systems (GPX1-8, GSTK1, GSTO1/2, PRDX5/6, TXN2, NQO1/2), and nucleotide metabolism (NME1-7, DGUOK, DTYMK, UCK1/2). The cluster is partially coherent around a 'metabolic enzyme' theme but is too large and contains functionally distant genes (neuronal receptors, WNT/SHH signaling, acute phase proteins) to be considered a tight functional module. This likely reflects a co-expression-based clustering that captures broadly expressed metabolic and mitochondrial genes across multiple tissue types.
recommended_followups: Sub-cluster the 1296 genes using stricter resolution to separate: (1) OXPHOS/mitoribosome core, (2) hepatic drug metabolism, (3) fatty acid oxidation, (4) neuronal receptor outliers

Check if GABR/GRIN1/GRM7 genes come from a specific batch or tissue sample type in the source dataset
Validate hepatocyte vs. neuron vs. muscle tissue-of-origin using cell-type deconvolution on the expression matrix
Assess whether BIRC5/CCNB1/RRM2 co-cluster reflects a proliferating subpopulation or technical co-expression artifact
Use DepMap CRISPR essentiality data to test whether OXPHOS subunit knockouts show correlated fitness effects consistent with complex membership
Investigate whether UGT1A1 polymorphism status (e.g., UGT1A1*28) in patient samples correlates with cluster activity score for irinotecan pharmacogenomics applications

clusters.title: Crystallin Lens Proteins – Alpha/Beta/Gamma Family
clusters.overall_function: Structural proteins of the ocular lens responsible for maintaining transparency and refractive properties; members of the beta-gamma crystallin superfamily expressed predominantly in lens fiber cells.
cell_type_relevance: Lens fiber cells (primary and secondary) – the dominant cell type expressing beta and gamma crystallins
Lens epithelial cells – may express lower levels of some beta crystallins
Highly specific to ocular lens lineage; not expected in other cell types under normal conditions
cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Strong predictor of ocular lens tissue origin

Could distinguish lens fiber cells from corneal, retinal, or other ocular cell types
cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: Crystallins are not canonical oncogenes; however, ectopic crystallin expression has been noted in some carcinomas (e.g., breast, lung) as stress-response proteins
Gamma crystallins in particular may appear in certain gliomas or retinoblastoma datasets
Low direct relevance for most cancer cell type classification tasks
cell_malignancy_status_prediction_releva: This cluster is predominantly associated with normal differentiated lens fiber cells, suggesting non-malignant status
Ectopic expression in a non-lens cancer context could indicate aberrant differentiation or stress response
Overall, high expression of this full cluster is more consistent with normal/benign lens tissue than malignant cells
drug_sensitivity_relevance: Limited direct pharmacological targets; crystallins are structural proteins without enzymatic activity

perturbation_modeling_relevance: Perturbation of individual crystallin genes (e.g., CRYBB2, CRYGD) models congenital cataract genetics
Co-expression and co-regulation of this cluster makes it useful for studying lens differentiation programs in perturbation screens

qc_warnings: All 11 members are beta or gamma crystallins – extremely tissue-restricted; if this cluster appears in a non-lens dataset, it may indicate contamination or doublets

clusters.rationale: All 11 genes belong to the beta-gamma crystallin superfamily (CRYBA2, CRYBA4, CRYBB1-3 are beta crystallins; CRYGA-D, CRYGN, CRYGS are gamma crystallins). These proteins are the primary structural components of the vertebrate lens, constituting the majority of lens protein content. Their co-clustering is biologically expected given shared tissue-specific expression in lens fiber cells, common regulatory transcription factors (MAF, PITX3), and structural/functional relatedness. The cluster is highly coherent and tissue-specific, making it an excellent marker for lens cell identity.
recommended_followups: Check for co-expression with CRYAA/CRYAB to assess whether alpha crystallins form a separate cluster or are absent from the dataset
Validate lens fiber cell identity by examining co-expression with MIP (aquaporin-0), LIM2, and BFSP1/2
If dataset is not lens-derived, investigate ambient RNA contamination or doublet rates
Examine regulatory network: test whether MAF or PITX3 perturbation collapses this entire cluster in perturbation modeling
Assess whether CRYGN (gamma-N, less characterized) clusters consistently with other gamma crystallins across datasets

clusters.title: CT45A Cancer-Testis Antigen Family Cluster
clusters.overall_function: This cluster comprises members of the CT45A (Cancer/Testis Antigen 45A) gene family, a group of X-linked cancer-testis antigens (CTAs) with restricted normal expression in testis and aberrant re-expression in various cancers. CT45A proteins are implicated in epigenetic regulation, DNA damage response, and promotion of tumor cell survival and metastasis.
cell_type_relevance: Germ cells / spermatogonia in normal testis (physiological expression)
Cancer cells with epigenetic derepression of X-linked CTAs (aberrant expression)
Cells undergoing DNA damage response or replication stress
Potentially cycling or proliferative tumor cell states
cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Testis (normal physiological expression context)
Ovarian cancer (CT45A members are well-documented in ovarian carcinoma)
Lung cancer and other epithelial malignancies where CTA re-expression is reported
Hematological malignancies such as multiple myeloma and Hodgkin lymphoma
cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: Ovarian carcinoma cells with CTA re-expression program
Multiple myeloma plasma cells
Hodgkin Reed-Sternberg cells
Broadly applicable as a marker of CTA-positive tumor cell states across carcinomas
cell_malignancy_status_prediction_releva: Strong indicator of malignant cells: CT45A genes are silenced in normal somatic tissues and re-expressed specifically in cancer cells via epigenetic derepression (DNA methylation loss)

Presence of CT45A expression can help distinguish malignant from non-malignant cells in mixed tumor microenvironment datasets

CT45A expression may correlate with sensitivity or resistance to platinum-based chemotherapy in ovarian cancer

Epigenetic perturbation experiments (DNMT inhibition, HDAC inhibition) would be expected to upregulate this cluster, making it a readout for epigenetic derepression
CRISPR screens targeting CT45A members could reveal roles in DNA damage checkpoint or replication stress pathways
Useful as a positive control gene set for cancer-testis antigen re-expression programs in perturbation atlases
qc_warnings: All 9 members are paralogs of the same gene family (CT45A1-CT45A10 minus CT45A4); clustering is expected due to high sequence and expression similarity — verify that co-clustering reflects biological co-regulation rather than mapping/alignment artifacts

High sequence similarity among paralogs may cause read mis-mapping in RNA-seq data, potentially inflating or deflating individual member counts
Expression of this cluster in non-testis, non-malignant cells should be treated as a QC flag for potential contamination or mis-annotation
clusters.rationale: All 9 entities are members of the CT45A (Cancer/Testis Antigen 45A) subfamily, a group of closely related X-linked paralogs encoded in a tandem array on chromosome Xq26.3. Their co-clustering is biologically coherent given shared promoter regulation via DNA methylation, high sequence homology, and coordinated re-expression in cancer. The cluster is highly specific to malignant contexts in somatic tissues, making it valuable for malignancy prediction, tissue-of-origin inference in cancers with CTA programs, and immunotherapy target identification. The absence of CT45A4 is a minor anomaly worth investigating. No housekeeping or lineage-mixing concerns are apparent.
recommended_followups: Verify CT45A4 absence: check if it was filtered due to low expression, missing annotation, or mapping issues
Cross-reference CT45A expression with DNA methylation data (RRBS/WGBS) to confirm epigenetic derepression mechanism
Assess co-expression with other CTA families (MAGE, GAGE, SSX) to define a broader CTA program module
Use CT45A cluster as a malignancy marker in cell type deconvolution of tumor microenvironment single-cell data
Investigate genetic interactions among CT45A paralogs using combinatorial CRISPR knockouts to assess functional redundancy

clusters.title: SSX Cancer-Testis Antigen Family

cell_type_relevance: Germ cells / spermatogonia in normal testis

Multiple myeloma and other hematologic malignancies
Lung, liver, and bladder cancers with CTA re-activation

Melanoma cells with CTA activation
Myeloma plasma cells
Sarcoma subtypes with epigenetic deregulation

clusters.rationale: All entities in this cluster are members of the SSX (Synovial Sarcoma X breakpoint) gene family, a well-characterized subfamily of cancer-testis antigens encoded on chromosome Xp11. The family includes SSX1 through SSX9 (with SSX2B and SSX4B as variant/retrogene copies). Their co-clustering is biologically coherent given shared sequence homology, co-localization on the X chromosome, shared epigenetic regulation via DNA methylation, and overlapping cancer-specific expression patterns. clusters.overall_function: This cluster consists entirely of pseudogenes (SSU72P2, SSU72P3, SSU72P4, SSU72P5, SSU72P7, SSU72P8) derived from SSU72, which encodes an RNA polymerase II CTD phosphatase involved in transcription termination and mRNA 3'-end processing. clusters.title: CDY/CDYL Chromodomain Y-Linked and Autosomal Histone Acetyltransferase/Chromatin Reader Family
clusters.overall_function: This cluster comprises the CDY (Chromodomain Y-linked) gene family and their autosomal paralogs CDYL and CDYL2. CDY1, CDY1B, CDY2A, CDY2B are Y-chromosome-encoded chromodomain proteins with histone crotonylase/acetyltransferase activity implicated in spermatogenesis and chromatin remodeling during male germ cell development. CDYL and CDYL2 are autosomal paralogs functioning as chromodomain-containing transcriptional corepressors that read H3K27me3 marks and interact with polycomb repressive complexes and REST/CoREST complexes to regulate gene silencing.

Pancreas: PDX1, NKX6-1, PAX4, NEUROD-related, MAFA, ISL1 point to pancreatic lineage
